operations.specification: Guest user registration endpoint that creates a temporary guest account without credentials. This operation allows unauthenticated visitors to obtain temporary access tokens to view published articles and comments on the discussion board. The guest account is created without requiring email or password authentication, providing immediate read-only access to the platform.
operations.name: join
operations.summary: Register an unauthenticated guest visitor for temporary read-only access to the discussion board.
operations.description:
The guest registration endpoint creates a temporary guest account that provides immediate read-only access to the discussion board platform. Guest users can view published articles and comments but cannot create content, post comments, upload attachments, or perform any write operations on the platform. This operation is designed to allow unauthenticated visitors to explore the discussion board without requiring account credentials.

Guest accounts are created with a temporary access token and refresh token that allow the user to maintain their session while browsing content. The system generates a unique identifier for each guest session, enabling the platform to track anonymous visitors while respecting their privacy and read-only access restrictions.

Guest users have restricted permissions that prevent them from accessing authenticated-only features. The discussion_board_guests table supports storing basic guest session information including created timestamp for session tracking and temporary token management.

The registration process is public and requires no authentication, making it accessible to any unauthenticated visitor. Guest accounts may have configurable session durations and can be managed through moderation tools if necessary.

Related operations include guest token refresh (GET /auth/guest/refresh) for maintaining active sessions and article retrieval endpoints (GET /articles) that respect guest user read-only permissions.

responseBody.description: Guest authorization response containing temporary access and refresh tokens.

operations.specification: Guest token refresh endpoint that renews temporary access tokens for existing guest sessions. This operation allows guest users to extend their temporary access by exchanging a valid refresh token for a new access token, enabling continuous browsing of published articles and comments without re-registration.
operations.name: refresh
operations.summary: Refresh temporary access tokens for an active guest session.
operations.description:
The guest token refresh endpoint enables guest users to renew their temporary access tokens without requiring re-registration. When a guest's access token expires, they can use their valid refresh token to obtain a new access token, allowing them to continue browsing published articles and comments on the discussion board.

Guest refresh tokens are short-lived credentials that authenticate the guest's existing session. The refresh operation validates the provided refresh token and, if valid, generates a new access token while potentially extending or rotating the refresh token itself. This mechanism allows guests to maintain continuous read-only access while providing security through token expiration.

The guest session information stored in the discussion_board_guests table is updated with new token information when refresh operations occur. The system tracks session lifecycle through timestamps, ensuring that abandoned guest sessions can be identified and cleaned up appropriately.

Guest refresh tokens are subject to configurable expiration windows and may be invalidated if suspicious activity is detected. The refresh operation maintains the same read-only access restrictions as the original guest registration, preventing any privilege escalation or write access.

This operation is a critical component of the guest user authentication flow, working in conjunction with the guest join operation (POST /auth/guest/join) to provide seamless temporary access management. Guest sessions refreshed through this endpoint retain their original created timestamp for session duration tracking.

responseBody.description: Guest authorization response containing renewed access and refresh tokens.

operations.specification: Member user registration endpoint for creating new discussion board accounts. This operation creates a new member record in the discussion_board_members table, generates initial authentication credentials, and issues JWT tokens (access and refresh) for immediate session establishment. The registration process accepts email, username, password, and display name, validates input constraints, checks for duplicate credentials (email and username must be unique), and sends email verification link. Upon successful registration, member account is created with account_status='active' and email_verified=false, requiring email verification before posting privileges are granted.
operations.name: join
operations.summary: Register a new member account for the discussion board.
operations.description:
This endpoint creates a new member account in the discussion_board_members table with complete authentication setup. The operation accepts member registration details including email, username, password, and display name. These credentials are validated against business rules: email must be valid format (max 254 characters) and globally unique, username must be 3-30 characters of alphanumeric characters plus hyphens/underscores and globally unique, password must meet complexity requirements, and display name must be 1-50 characters.

The password is immediately hashed using bcrypt with minimum 12 rounds before storage, never storing plain text. The newly created member record is initialized with email_verified=false, account_status='active', and created_at timestamp set to current UTC time. A verification email is generated and sent to the provided email address containing a verification link that member must click to enable article creation and comment posting capabilities.

Upon successful account creation, the operation generates JWT tokens including an access token (short-lived, used for immediate API requests) and a refresh token (long-lived, used to obtain new access tokens). These tokens are issued immediately allowing the newly registered member to interact with the platform, though posting restrictions remain until email verification is completed.

The email field is stored exactly as provided and must not already exist in the discussion_board_members table (unique constraint). The username field is enforced case-insensitive and must not already exist. The display_name field is stored as provided and is displayed publicly as author attribution on articles and comments. The password_hash field stores the bcrypt-hashed result and is never returned to the client.

This operation should be called before any authenticated member operations. Related operations include login for existing members, refresh for token renewal, and email verification endpoints for activating posting privileges after registration.

requestBody.description: Member registration credentials including email, username, password, and display name

responseBody.description: Newly created member account with authentication tokens

operations.specification: Member user login endpoint for authenticating existing discussion board members. This operation validates provided credentials (email or username with password) against the discussion_board_members table, verifies account status permits login, validates password against stored bcrypt hash, and upon successful authentication creates a new session record in discussion_board_member_sessions table with connection context (IP address, URL, referrer). The operation then issues JWT tokens (access and refresh) that grant authentication context to subsequent API requests.
operations.name: login
operations.summary: Authenticate a member and establish a new session.
operations.description:
This endpoint authenticates an existing member by validating credentials and establishing an authenticated session. The operation accepts either email or username as the login identifier, along with the member's password. The identifier is matched case-insensitively against the discussion_board_members table to locate the member account.

Password validation compares the provided plain text password against the stored password_hash field using bcrypt verification. Passwords must match exactly to authentication to succeed. The account_status field is checked to ensure the member account is in 'active' state; accounts with status 'suspended', 'terminated', or 'deleted' are rejected with appropriate error responses.

Upon successful credential validation, a new session record is created in the discussion_board_member_sessions table capturing connection metadata: the ip field records the IPv4 or IPv6 address of the login request, the href field captures the full URL where login occurred, and the referrer field captures the HTTP Referrer header (may be empty string if unavailable). The session created_at timestamp is set to current UTC time, and expired_at remains null for active sessions. Sessions automatically expire after 7 days.

The email_verified field of the member is checked to determine posting privileges. Members with email_verified=false can access the platform but have restrictions on creating articles and posting comments until verification is completed. The last_login_at field is updated to the current timestamp for activity tracking.

JWT tokens are issued upon successful login: an access token (short-lived, typically valid for 15 minutes) used for authenticating subsequent API requests, and a refresh token (long-lived, valid for 7 days) used to obtain new access tokens without re-entering credentials. Both tokens are issued to the client for secure token-based authentication.

This operation should be called by members with existing accounts. Related operations include join for new member registration, refresh for obtaining new access tokens, and logout for terminating the current session.

requestBody.description: Member login credentials (email or username with password)

responseBody.description: Authenticated member with new session and JWT tokens

operations.specification: Member token refresh endpoint for renewing access tokens using a valid refresh token. This operation validates the provided refresh token, verifies the session is still active (expired_at is null), confirms member account status permits access, and issues a new access token with extended validity. The refresh token itself remains valid for continued use until the 7-day expiration window closes or member explicitly logs out.
operations.name: refresh
operations.summary: Refresh member access token using a valid refresh token.
operations.description:
This endpoint renews a member's access token when the current access token has expired or is about to expire. The operation accepts a refresh token issued during login or previous refresh operations, validates its signature and claims, and confirms the associated session is still active.

The refresh token is verified to belong to a valid session record in the discussion_board_member_sessions table. The session's expired_at field is checked to ensure the session has not been manually terminated (expired_at must be null for active sessions). Sessions that have expired_at set to a non-null timestamp are rejected as the session has been explicitly ended.

The associated member's discussion_board_member_id is retrieved from the session, and the member record is validated to ensure account_status is 'active'. Members with status 'suspended', 'terminated', or 'deleted' cannot refresh tokens. The last_login_at field of the member is NOT updated on refresh operations, only on actual login.

The refresh token itself has a 7-day validity window from creation. If the refresh token has expired (created_at + 7 days has passed), the operation is rejected and the member must log in again. The token validity is tied to the session's created_at timestamp.

Upon successful validation, a new access token is issued with the same or extended validity period (typically 15 minutes). The refresh token remains valid and can be used multiple times until it expires naturally after 7 days or the associated session is explicitly terminated by logout.

This operation enables seamless member experience by allowing token renewal without requiring re-authentication. It should be called automatically by client applications when access tokens approach expiration. Related operations include login for initial authentication, logout for terminating the session, and other member operations that require valid access tokens.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining a new access token

responseBody.description: New access token for continued authentication

operations.specification: Generate moderator registration API operation that allows creation of new moderator accounts. This operation corresponds to the discussion_board_moderators Prisma table. Moderators are administrative users who authenticate separately from members with their own credentials. This join operation creates a new moderator account with required authentication credentials (email, username, password_hash) and stores the moderator in the system with active status.
operations.name: join
operations.summary: Register a new moderator account in the discussion board system.
operations.description:
The moderator registration endpoint enables creation of new administrative accounts for users who will perform content moderation and user management tasks. This operation creates a new record in the discussion_board_moderators table with the provided credentials, including email, username, password_hash, and display_name fields from the schema.

Moderators authenticate separately from regular members using their own unique credentials. The registration process validates that the email and username are unique across all moderators (as enforced by unique constraints in the discussion_board_moderators table). The password is hashed using bcrypt with minimum 12 rounds for security before being stored in the password_hash field.

The operation initializes a new moderator account with account_status set to 'active', granting full moderator privileges immediately upon account creation. The system records the creation timestamp in created_at and sets updated_at to the same value. The display_name field captures the moderator's identification name that will appear in audit logs and moderation actions.

This is a public endpoint allowing initial moderator account creation. The response returns an authorization token (access and refresh tokens) via the IDiscussionBoardModerator.IAuthorized response type, enabling the newly registered moderator to authenticate and access moderation features immediately.

Related operations: moderator login endpoint for existing account authentication, token refresh endpoint for maintaining active sessions.

requestBody.description: Registration credentials and moderator information for creating a new moderator account.

responseBody.description: Moderator authorization credentials including JWT access token and refresh token for authenticated moderator sessions.

operations.specification: Generate moderator login API operation for authenticating existing moderator accounts. This operation corresponds to the discussion_board_moderators Prisma table. Moderators authenticate using their email or username along with password credentials. This login operation validates credentials against stored password_hash in the moderators table and establishes an authenticated session stored in discussion_board_moderator_sessions table.
operations.name: login
operations.summary: Authenticate a moderator and establish an authenticated session.
operations.description:
The moderator login endpoint authenticates administrative users by validating their credentials against stored authentication data in the discussion_board_moderators table. Moderators provide either their email or username along with their password. The system retrieves the moderator record using the provided email or username identifier and validates the provided password against the stored password_hash field using bcrypt verification.

Upon successful authentication, the system validates that the moderator's account_status is 'active', ensuring only active moderators can establish authenticated sessions. The account_status field controls access, preventing login for inactive or terminated moderator accounts.

The authentication process creates a new session record in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table, capturing security context including the IP address, HTTP referrer, and the full URL/href from which the login occurred. These session details are critical for security monitoring of administrative access and detecting unauthorized login attempts from unusual IP addresses or referrers.

The response returns JWT authentication credentials (access token and refresh token) via the IDiscussionBoardModerator.IAuthorized response type. The access token enables the moderator to perform administrative tasks, while the refresh token allows extending the session lifetime without requiring re-authentication.

Sessions expire automatically after 7 days or upon explicit logout. The system tracks login history through the created_at timestamp in the moderator_sessions table and last_login_at field in the moderators table.

Related operations: moderator join endpoint for account creation, token refresh endpoint for session extension.

requestBody.description: Login credentials (email or username and password) for moderator authentication.

responseBody.description: Moderator authorization credentials including JWT access token and refresh token for authenticated moderator sessions.

operations.specification: Generate token refresh API operation for extending moderator session lifetime. This operation corresponds to the discussion_board_moderator_sessions Prisma table. Moderators can refresh their authentication tokens using a valid refresh token to maintain active sessions without requiring password re-entry. The operation validates the refresh token and issues new access/refresh token pair.
operations.name: refresh
operations.summary: Refresh moderator authentication tokens and extend session lifetime.
operations.description:
The moderator token refresh endpoint enables extending moderator session lifetimes by exchanging a valid refresh token for new access and refresh tokens. This operation allows moderators to maintain continuous authentication without requiring password re-entry when their access token expires.

The refresh operation validates the provided refresh token against active sessions in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table. The system verifies that the session has not expired (expired_at is null) and that the associated moderator account in discussion_board_moderators has account_status of 'active', ensuring terminated or inactive moderators cannot extend their sessions.

Upon successful validation, the operation returns new JWT credentials (access token and refresh token) via the IDiscussionBoardModerator.IAuthorized response type. The new tokens enable continued administrative access without disruption. The original session in discussion_board_moderator_sessions remains active with its original created_at timestamp, preserving the session creation history for audit purposes.

The refresh token mechanism provides enhanced security by separating long-lived refresh tokens from short-lived access tokens. Access tokens are used for API requests and are brief-lived, while refresh tokens are used only for token renewal and can have longer expiration (7 days). This allows secure token rotation without requiring moderators to re-authenticate with passwords repeatedly.

The operation does not modify the discussion_board_moderator_sessions record; it only validates the session is active and the moderator is active, then issues new tokens. Session termination occurs only through explicit logout or automatic expiration after 7 days of inactivity.

Related operations: moderator login endpoint for initial authentication, moderator join endpoint for account creation.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for extending moderator authentication session.

responseBody.description: Moderator authorization credentials including refreshed JWT access token and refresh token.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a filtered, paginated, and sorted list of discussion board articles. It operates on the discussion_board_articles table and supports advanced search capabilities including filtering by status, category, member/creator, and date ranges. The operation implements pagination with configurable page sizes and offset-based navigation, along with sorting by creation date, publication date, title, or view count in ascending or descending order. Full-text search across article titles and body content is supported through GIN indexes.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of discussion board articles

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of discussion board articles from the system. This operation provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for discovering articles based on multiple criteria including publication status (pending_approval, published, rejected, archived), assigned category, article creator/member, date ranges, and full-text search across article titles and body content.

The operation supports sophisticated pagination with configurable page sizes (default 20, max 100) and offset-based navigation for efficient data retrieval. Results can be sorted by creation timestamp, publication timestamp, article title, or view count in ascending or descending order. Multiple sort criteria can be chained for complex ordering requirements.

Articles returned in search results include essential metadata (title, status, creator info, category, timestamps, view count) optimized for list display. The response includes pagination metadata allowing clients to determine total article count, current page position, and navigation to next/previous pages. Article body content is truncated for list views to improve performance.

Security and authorization are enforced based on article status and user authentication. Unauthenticated users see only published articles. Members see published articles plus their own articles in any status. Moderators see all articles regardless of status for review and management purposes. Soft-deleted articles (deleted_at is not null) are excluded from public views but visible to moderators.

operations.specification: This operation creates a new discussion board article in the discussion_board_articles table. A member submits article content (title, body, and optional category) which is initially placed in 'pending_approval' status. The article is assigned to the authenticated member as the creator. Category assignment is required and must reference an existing category from discussion_board_categories table. Upon successful creation, the article record is persisted with timestamps, initialized view_count to 0, and null values for rejection_reason, published_at, and deleted_at. The operation enforces validation rules on title (5-200 characters), body (10-50,000 characters), and category existence.
operations.summary: Create a new discussion board article in pending approval status
operations.description:
Create a new discussion board article to initiate a discussion thread on the platform. This operation allows authenticated members to submit article content for moderator review before publication. The article is created in 'pending_approval' status, meaning it is not visible to other users until a moderator reviews and approves it.

The operation requires three essential inputs: article title (5-200 characters), article body content (10-50,000 characters containing the main discussion text), and category selection from predefined categories (Economics, Politics, Economic Policy, Political Analysis, Other). The authenticated member making the request is automatically assigned as the article creator/author. The article is assigned a unique UUID identifier upon creation.

Initial article state includes creation timestamp (set to current UTC time), updated_at also set to creation time, view_count initialized to 0, and null values for rejection_reason, published_at, and deleted_at. The operation validates that the selected category exists in the discussion_board_categories table before creating the article.

This operation requires authentication - only verified members can create articles. The member's email must be verified (email_verified = true) and account status must be 'active'. Articles submitted by members undergo moderator review workflow where moderators can approve (status → published), reject (status → rejected with optional rejection_reason), request changes, or delete the article. Members can edit their pending articles before moderation approval, and can resubmit rejected articles after revisions.

responseBody.description: Newly created article with all assigned metadata including timestamps, status, and creator information

The article includes complete details about the discussion topic including title, body content, current status, view count, and moderation information. The retrieved article contains full context needed for displaying the article detail view including creator information, category assignment, and publication timeline.

Retrieve complete details of a single discussion board article from the discussion_board_articles table. This operation fetches the article by its unique identifier and returns comprehensive information including the article title, body content, current publication status, view count, moderation status, rejection reason (if applicable), and timestamps for creation, modification, and publication.

The retrieved article includes metadata about the creator member, assigned category, and moderation workflow state. Articles flow through a moderation process before publication, with possible statuses including pending_approval (awaiting moderator review), published (approved and visible), rejected (did not meet guidelines), and archived (hidden from public view). Rejection reasons are included for rejected articles to help creators understand why their submission was not approved.

This operation enforces appropriate access control based on article status and user role. Published articles are accessible to all users, while pending and rejected articles may be restricted to the article creator and moderators depending on business requirements. Archived articles may require special permissions or may be restricted entirely from regular member access.

View count tracking is maintained separately and reflects the number of times this article detail page has been accessed. Each successful retrieval of this endpoint should increment the view counter to track article engagement metrics. The operation returns all core article fields from the discussion_board_articles table including id, title, body, status, view_count, rejection_reason, created_at, updated_at, published_at, deleted_at, discussion_board_member_id, and discussion_board_category_id.

The operation supports partial updates where only specified fields are modified. Status updates may trigger moderation workflow state changes (e.g., moving from published back to pending_approval for re-review). This operation enforces authorization checks to ensure only the article creator or moderators can modify articles.
operations.summary: Update an existing discussion board article
operations.description:
Update an existing discussion board article in the discussion_board_articles table. This operation allows modification of article attributes including title, body content, category assignment, and status. The operation enforces strict authorization - typically only the article creator can edit their own articles, with moderators having additional authority to change status and add rejection reasons.

When an article is updated, the updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed to record the modification time. However, the created_at and published_at timestamps remain immutable and are never modified, preserving the audit trail of when the article was originally created and officially published by moderators.

Title must remain between 5 and 200 characters, and body content must remain between 10 and 50,000 characters. These validation constraints are enforced to maintain content quality standards. Category assignments are validated to ensure the referenced discussion_board_category_id exists in the categories table. Status updates follow the workflow rules - articles can transition between pending_approval, published, rejected, and archived states based on moderation actions.

Rejection reasons can be updated or added when an article is in rejected status, providing creators with detailed feedback about why their submission did not meet guidelines. Rejection reasons must not exceed 500 characters. When moderators request changes or reject articles, they may include detailed explanations to guide creators toward acceptable content.

This operation triggers automatic soft deletion behaviors when requested - if the article's deletion is intended, the deleted_at timestamp may be set through status changes or explicit deletion operations. The operation returns the complete updated article record reflecting all changes.

operations.summary: Delete a discussion board article by ID
operations.description:
Permanently remove an article from the discussion board system. This operation allows authorized users (article author or moderators) to delete published or draft articles. The deletion is permanent and cannot be undone through the API.

Security and Authorization: Only the article's original author or users with moderator privileges can delete an article. The system verifies ownership and permissions before processing the deletion request. Attempting to delete another user's article without appropriate permissions will result in a forbidden access error.

Impact on Related Data: When an article is deleted, the article record is completely removed from the database. Comments associated with the deleted article may be retained in an orphaned state or deleted based on the system's cascade delete configuration. The deletion is recorded in the system audit trail for moderation and compliance purposes.

Error Handling: The operation returns a 404 error if the specified article does not exist, a 403 error if the requesting user lacks permission to delete the article, and a 409 error if the article cannot be deleted due to system constraints.

This operation allows authenticated members to post comments in response to an article, enabling direct engagement and discussion. The comment is published immediately without requiring moderator approval, ensuring real-time visibility and immediate community response. Each comment belongs exclusively to one article and extends that article's discussion thread. The creating member's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token.
operations.summary: Create a new comment on a discussion board article
operations.description:
Create and publish a new comment on a discussion board article, enabling members to share perspectives, ask questions, and respond to article content. Comments are published immediately upon creation without requiring moderator approval, creating immediate visibility for community engagement.

The comment body must be between 1 and 5,000 characters and supports plain text with basic formatting. Comments can include file and image attachments that are uploaded separately or embedded within the content. The creating member's identity is automatically populated from the authenticated JWT token.

Display name updates are reflected in the member's public profile attribution on articles and comments. Account status can be modified to control member access (values: 'active', 'suspended', 'terminated', 'deleted'). When account_status is set to 'deleted', the deleted_at timestamp is automatically set, implementing soft deletion for audit trail and data retention purposes.

operations.summary: Delete a discussion board member account permanently
operations.description:
Delete a registered member account from the discussion board system, removing all member authentication credentials and profile information. This operation removes the member record from the discussion_board_members table, effectively terminating the account and access to the platform.

The deletion process removes the member's email, username, password hash, and all authentication-related data. The operation validates that the requested member exists before attempting deletion and ensures proper authorization - only the member themselves (via authenticated session) or system administrators can delete an account.

This is an irreversible operation that permanently removes member records from the system. The member will no longer be able to authenticate or access the platform after deletion. Any articles or comments created by the member may remain in the system with orphaned author references, depending on application-level cascade policies for content deletion.

Authorization context: The operation requires authentication and validates that the requesting user is either the member being deleted (self-deletion) or has administrative privileges. Attempts to delete other members' accounts without proper authorization will be rejected.

Profile pictures are automatically resized to 200x200 pixels and EXIF metadata is stripped during upload for privacy protection. The bio field can contain information relevant to the economic and political discussion topics of the platform.

The profile record is created automatically when a member account is created and maintains a 1:1 relationship with the discussion_board_members table. The created_at timestamp indicates when the profile was created (typically when the member account was registered), and updated_at tracks the most recent modification to any profile field.

This operation is public and does not require authentication, allowing all users (including guests) to view member profile information. The profile data supports community interaction by helping users understand other members' backgrounds and expertise relevant to discussions.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete preference settings for a specific member from the discussion board platform. This operation fetches all notification and display preferences configured for the member, allowing clients to display current preference state or enable preference management interfaces.

The member preferences are identified by the memberId path parameter which must correspond to a valid discussion_board_members record. Each member has exactly one preference record that is automatically created with sensible defaults when the member account is created. The preferences include comprehensive notification controls with individual toggles for email notifications (master control), comment reply notifications, article reply notifications, article approval notifications, and moderator action notifications. Members can also opt into optional daily digest emails that summarize new articles and discussions.

Display preferences include theme selection with valid options of 'light', 'dark', or 'system' (which follows the user's system preference). These preferences are independent of profile data, maintaining clear separation between public identity information stored in member profiles and private settings stored in member preferences. The operation returns all preference fields including created_at and updated_at timestamps that track when the preference record was created and last modified, providing an audit trail of preference changes.

The endpoint allows authenticated members to modify their email notification settings (article replies, comment replies, approval notifications, moderator action notifications, daily digest), display theme preference (light/dark/system), and other personal settings. All preference modifications must include only valid preference fields; invalid or unknown fields are rejected.

Preference validation ensures that all boolean notification preference fields (email_notifications_enabled, comment_reply_notifications, article_reply_notifications, article_approval_notifications, moderator_action_notifications, daily_digest_enabled) are either true or false. The display_theme preference must be one of the valid values: 'light', 'dark', or 'system'. Invalid theme values are rejected with descriptive error messages.

When preferences are successfully updated, the system records the change timestamp in the updated_at field to track when preferences were last modified. This timestamp is useful for audit trails and understanding when members made preference changes. The operation returns the complete updated preference object reflecting all current settings after the update is applied.

operations.specification: This operation updates the member's password for an authenticated member in the discussion_board_members table. The endpoint requires the member to provide their current password for verification and a new password that meets all password complexity requirements (minimum 8 characters, uppercase, lowercase, numeric, and special character). The operation validates that the memberId path parameter matches the authenticated user's ID to prevent cross-member password changes. Password updates trigger immediate session invalidation across all devices to force re-authentication. The new password is hashed using bcrypt with salt rounds of 12 minimum before storage. This operation does not allow password reuse - the system prevents setting a password that matches any of the user's last 3 passwords.
operations.description:
Update the password for an authenticated member's account.

This operation allows members to change their password stored in the discussion_board_members table. The member must provide their current password (for verification that they have legitimate access to the account) and a new password that meets all password complexity requirements. The current password is verified by comparing its bcrypt hash against the stored password_hash field.

Password requirements are strictly enforced: minimum 8 characters in length, must contain at least one uppercase letter (A-Z), at least one lowercase letter (a-z), at least one numeric digit (0-9), and at least one special character from the set (!@#$%^&*). The system rejects passwords that are fewer than 8 characters, lack required character types, exceed 128 characters, contain the username, contain the email address.

The authenticated member can only update their own password by providing their memberId in the path. The system validates that the memberId path parameter matches the authenticated user's ID to prevent unauthorized password changes on other accounts. When the incorrect current password is provided, the operation denies the change and returns an error without revealing the nature of the mismatch.

Upon successful password change, the system immediately invalidates all existing authentication sessions for that member across all devices and browsers. This forces the member to re-authenticate on all connected devices using their new password, which is a critical security measure. The new password is hashed using bcrypt with a minimum of 12 salt rounds before being stored in the password_hash field. The system prevents password reuse by checking against the member's last 3 passwords - if the new password matches any recent password, the change is rejected.

The operation updates the discussion_board_members.updated_at timestamp to record when the password was changed. Password change operations are logged for security audit purposes. The operation does not return the password or password hash in the response - only confirmation of successful change.

Related operations: PUT /memberPreferences/{memberId} allows updating notification and display preferences separately from password security changes.

operations.specification: This operation updates a member's email address in the discussion_board_members table. The operation requires the authenticated member to provide their current password for verification before allowing the email change. A new email address must be provided, and it must be validated for proper email format and uniqueness across all member accounts. Upon successful email change, the system generates a new email verification code that is sent to the new email address. The member must verify the new email before the change becomes fully active, during which time the old email remains the active login credential. This operation maps directly to the discussion_board_members table and updates the email field while maintaining security by requiring password confirmation.
operations.summary: Update a member's email address with verification requirement
operations.description:
Update the email address associated with a member account in the discussion board system. This is a security-sensitive operation that requires the member to verify their current password before the email can be changed. The new email address must be validated for proper format and uniqueness to prevent duplicate registrations.

When a member initiates an email change, the system validates that the provided email address is in valid RFC 5322 format and that no other member account is already using this email address. The email must not exceed 254 characters. After validation, the system records the new email address in the discussion_board_members table.

Email verification is required for the email change to take full effect. Upon successful email update, the system generates a unique verification token and code valid for 24 hours, then sends a verification email to the new address containing a clickable verification link and alphanumeric verification code. Until the member verifies the new email address, the previous email remains the active login credential.

Once the member verifies the new email through the verification link or code entry, the system marks the email_verified flag as true for the member account. All future authentication and password recovery operations use the newly verified email address.

This operation is restricted to authenticated members and can only be performed on the member's own account. The operation requires the current password as an additional security measure to prevent unauthorized email hijacking. All email changes are logged in the audit trail with the timestamp and member identity for security monitoring and account recovery purposes.

operations.specification: This operation handles uploading a profile picture for a member account stored in the discussion_board_member_profiles and discussion_board_attachments tables. The operation accepts an image file upload from an authenticated member and stores it in the attachment system. The image file must be in JPG, PNG, GIF, or WebP format and not exceed 5 MB in size. The system automatically resizes the image to 200x200 pixels for consistent profile display across the platform. Upon successful upload, the system updates the discussion_board_member_profiles table with the profile_picture_url field pointing to the newly stored image, and creates a corresponding attachment record in discussion_board_attachments with parent_type='profile' and the member's profile as the parent. The operation returns the updated member profile with the new profile picture URL.
operations.summary: Upload and set a profile picture for a member account
operations.description:
Upload a profile picture for a member's discussion board account. This operation allows authenticated members to upload a new profile picture that will be displayed with their articles, comments, and public profile page throughout the platform.

The profile picture must be an image file in one of the supported formats: JPG, PNG, GIF, or WebP. The file size must not exceed 5 MB. The system validates the file type by inspecting the file header (magic number) rather than relying on file extension for security purposes. Upon upload, the system automatically processes the image: resizing it to a standard 200x200 pixel dimension for consistent display, stripping any EXIF metadata to protect privacy, and computing a SHA-256 hash of the file content for integrity verification.

The uploaded image is stored in the secure attachment storage system with a system-generated filename following the pattern timestamp_hash_originalname to prevent directory traversal attacks and ensure unique storage paths. The original filename provided by the member is preserved for audit purposes.

Upon successful upload, the system updates the member's profile record in the discussion_board_member_profiles table, setting the profile_picture_url field to point to the newly stored image. A corresponding attachment record is created in the discussion_board_attachments table with parent_type='profile' to track all profile picture uploads for audit purposes. The operation is restricted to authenticated members and can only be performed on the member's own profile picture.

If the member already has a profile picture, the new upload replaces the previous image. The previous image file may be automatically cleaned up from storage after a grace period. If the member wants to remove their profile picture entirely, they would need to use a separate delete operation rather than uploading a blank or placeholder image.

The operation returns the updated member profile information including the new profile_picture_url, allowing the client to immediately display the uploaded picture to confirm successful upload.

The operation updates the member's profile updated_at timestamp to track the modification.
operations.summary: Delete a member's profile picture from their discussion board profile
operations.description:
Remove the profile picture associated with a specific member account. This operation sets the profile_picture_url field to null in the discussion_board_member_profiles table, causing the member's avatar to revert to a system default placeholder.

Authentication and authorization are enforced to ensure members can only delete their own profile pictures. Attempting to delete another member's profile picture returns a 403 Forbidden error with message "You do not have permission to modify this profile."

The profile_picture_url field in discussion_board_member_profiles stores a URI reference to the member's profile picture. When deleted, this field becomes null, and the system displays the default avatar in all locations where the member's profile picture appears (article author attribution, comment author display, profile view, etc.).

Upon successful deletion, the profile's updated_at timestamp is updated to the current UTC time, creating an audit trail of the modification. The operation does not delete the actual image file from storage—that cleanup happens asynchronously after confirmation that no other references exist.

If the member has no profile picture currently set (profile_picture_url is already null), the operation succeeds with HTTP 200 OK, treating it as an idempotent operation. No error is returned for deleting a non-existent profile picture.

operations.specification: This operation terminates the authenticated member's current session by invalidating the JWT refresh token and clearing authentication credentials. The operation targets the discussion_board_member_sessions table, marking the session's expired_at field with the current timestamp. This implements secure logout functionality that invalidates the user's authentication across all API requests. The operation must receive a valid access token in the Authorization header and uses the authenticated user's ID extracted from the token claims.
operations.summary: Logout an authenticated member and terminate their current session
operations.description:
Terminate the authenticated member's current session and invalidate their authentication credentials. This operation marks the session record in discussion_board_member_sessions as expired by setting the expired_at timestamp to the current UTC time.

Authentication is required for this operation. The member must provide a valid JWT access token in the Authorization header (Bearer scheme). The authenticated user's member ID is extracted from the token claims (JWT sub claim or user context) and used to identify which session to terminate.

When logout is processed, the system performs the following actions: (1) Locate the member's active session (where expired_at is null), (2) Set the expired_at field to current timestamp, (3) Blacklist the member's refresh token to prevent reuse, (4) Clear any session cookies on the client side (via Set-Cookie header with Max-Age=0), (5) Record the logout event in audit logs with timestamp.

After logout succeeds, the member must authenticate again by providing email/username and password to obtain new tokens. All subsequent API requests using the invalidated access token will return HTTP 401 Unauthorized with message "Token expired or invalid. Please log in again."

The operation supports concurrent sessions—logging out from one device/browser only invalidates that specific session. Other active sessions on different devices remain valid and unaffected. For example, if a member is logged in on desktop and mobile, logout on desktop invalidates only the desktop session; the mobile session remains active.

If the member has no active session (all sessions already have expired_at timestamps), the operation still succeeds with HTTP 200 OK, treating logout as idempotent. No error is returned for logging out when already logged out.

WHEN a member's password is changed, THE system SHALL invalidate all refresh tokens associated with that member account, forcing re-login on all devices.

operations.specification: This operation verifies a member's email address using a verification token or code sent during registration. The operation validates the provided token/code against stored verification data, checks expiration, and marks the member's email as verified in the discussion_board_members table. Upon successful verification, the member gains full posting privileges (ability to create articles and post comments). This operation is associated with the discussion_board_members table and supports the email verification workflow required before members can participate in discussions.
operations.summary: Verify a member's email address using verification token or code
operations.description:
This operation completes the email verification process for newly registered members. When a member registers, the system sends a verification email containing a unique token or alphanumeric code. This endpoint allows the member to submit that token or code to prove ownership of their email address.

The verification process is critical to the discussion board's security and participation model. Members with unverified emails cannot create articles or post comments, ensuring only legitimate email addresses are used for account creation. The system must validate that the provided token or code matches stored verification data and has not expired (24-hour validity window).

Upon successful verification, the system updates the discussion_board_members table, setting email_verified to true. This immediately enables the member to create articles and post comments. The verification token is cleared from storage after successful use to prevent replay attacks.

If verification fails (invalid code, expired code, or already verified), the system returns a specific error message indicating the issue. Expired tokens trigger an offer to resend verification email, making the recovery path clear to users.

This operation requires member authentication context to identify which member is verifying their email. The authenticated member submitting the request must match the member_id associated with the verification data. This prevents one member from verifying another member's email address.

Related operations: POST /auth/member/resend-verification (to request new verification email if code expires), which shares the same workflow context and may be called before or after this verification attempt.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of successful email verification with member details

operations.specification: This operation generates and sends a new verification email to a member's registered email address. The operation creates a fresh verification token (valid for 24 hours) and alphanumeric code, invalidating any previous verification code. The new verification email is sent containing both the token (for link-based verification) and code (for manual entry). This operation is associated with the discussion_board_members table and supports the email verification workflow when original verification emails are lost or the token expires.
operations.summary: Request a new email verification code and email
operations.description:
This operation handles the resend verification email workflow for members who lost the original verification email, entered an incorrect code too many times, or the original verification code expired (24-hour validity window). Members can request a new verification email containing a fresh token and code.

The operation enforces rate limiting to prevent abuse—members can request resend at most once per 5 minutes per account. If a member attempts to resend more frequently, the system returns an error message indicating they must wait before requesting another verification email.

When a resend is requested, the system generates a new verification token and code, invalidating the previous token/code pair. This prevents confusion from multiple valid tokens in circulation. The new verification email is sent immediately to the member's registered email address with clear instructions for completing verification.

The resend operation updates the verification data in the discussion_board_members table (or verification tracking table if implemented separately). The email_verified flag remains false until successful verification using the new code. The member continues to have read-only access but cannot create articles or post comments until email verification is completed.

This operation requires member authentication to identify which member is requesting the resend. The authenticated member submitting the request must have an account in discussion_board_members with unverified status (email_verified = false). Members with already-verified emails can still call this endpoint, which returns a success message for security reasons (preventing account enumeration attacks).

Rate limiting context: Failed attempts to resend (due to rate limiting) should be tracked separately from successful resends. The 5-minute window resets from the timestamp of the most recent resend request by that member.

operations.specification: This operation initiates the password reset workflow for a member who has forgotten their password. operations.summary: Request password reset via email for a discussion board member account
operations.description:
Initiates the password reset workflow for members who have forgotten their password. When a member provides their email address, the system validates that an account exists with that email, generates a cryptographically secure password reset token with 1-hour expiration, and sends a password reset email containing a secure reset link and instructions.

Security considerations: The system deliberately does not reveal whether an account exists with the provided email address. This prevents account enumeration attacks where bad actors could discover which email addresses are registered. The confirmation message displayed to the user is identical regardless of whether the email exists in the system.

The password reset token is valid for exactly 1 hour from generation. After 1 hour, the token expires and the user must request a new password reset. The reset token is stored securely and validated when the user clicks the reset link in their email.

This operation relates to the discussion_board_members table, specifically the email field which must match exactly (case-insensitive) and the password_hash field which will be updated when the member confirms the reset. The system records the password reset request timestamp for security audit purposes.

The password reset workflow is the first step in a two-step process. After the member receives the email and clicks the reset link, they proceed to the password-reset-confirm endpoint to set their new password. The reset token ensures that only the member who owns the email address can complete the password reset.

Rate limiting is enforced to prevent abuse: members can request password reset emails a maximum of once per 5 minutes per email address.

operations.specification: This operation completes the password reset workflow for a member who has received a password reset email. The endpoint accepts a valid password reset token, the new password, and password confirmation. The system validates the reset token (not expired, not already used), verifies the new password meets all complexity requirements, hashes the new password, updates the member's password_hash in the discussion_board_members table, invalidates all existing sessions for that member, and sends a confirmation email. This operation is the second step in the password recovery flow specified in user account management requirements.
operations.summary: Confirm password reset and set new password for a discussion board member
operations.description:
Completes the password reset workflow by validating the reset token received in the password reset email and allowing the member to set a new password. When a member clicks the reset link in their email, they are directed to a form containing the reset token. The member enters a new password and confirmation, then submits this operation.

Token validation: The system validates that the reset token is valid (matches stored token), has not expired (1-hour window from request), and has not been previously used. If the token is invalid or expired, the operation returns an error directing the member to request a new password reset.

Password requirements enforcement: The new password must meet all complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters, at least one uppercase letter, at least one lowercase letter, at least one numeric digit, at least one special character from {!@#$%^&*}. The password cannot contain the member's email address or username. The password cannot match any of the member's last 3 passwords (password reuse prevention). If the new password fails any requirement, the operation returns a specific error message indicating which requirements are not met.

Password confirmation: The new password must exactly match the password confirmation field. If they do not match, the operation returns an error and requires the user to re-enter both password fields.

Database updates: Upon successful validation, the system hashes the new password using bcrypt with minimum 12 salt rounds and updates the password_hash field in the discussion_board_members table. The updated_at timestamp is updated to the current time. The reset token is invalidated (removed from storage) to prevent reuse.

Session invalidation: All existing authentication sessions for the member are immediately terminated. This forces the member to log in again on all devices using their new password. All existing JWT refresh tokens are blacklisted.

Notification: A confirmation email is sent to the member's registered email address confirming that their password has been reset.

Relationship to discussion_board_members table: This operation updates the password_hash and updated_at fields for the member identified by the reset token. The operation indirectly affects discussion_board_member_sessions table by invalidating sessions.

This is the second operation in a two-step password reset process. The password-reset-request operation must be executed first to generate and email the reset token.

Upon successful password change, all existing sessions for the member are invalidated, forcing re-authentication on all devices for security purposes. Allows an authenticated member to change their account password securely. The member must provide their current password for verification to prevent unauthorized password changes. The new password must meet all complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters, at least one uppercase letter, at least one lowercase letter, at least one numeric digit, and at least one special character from the set: !@#$%^&*. The new password must not be a commonly used password or contain the member's username or email address.

Each member can maintain multiple concurrent sessions across different devices; deleting one session affects only that specific device/login context while preserving other active sessions. The operation is idempotent - attempting to delete an already-expired session returns success without error.

Any outstanding access tokens remain valid until their natural expiration (15 minutes); only the refresh token becomes invalid. This operation validates whether a provided JWT access token is authentic, unmodified, and currently valid. The operation accepts a JWT access token in the request body and performs comprehensive validation checks. First, it verifies the token signature using the server's HMAC signing secret, ensuring the token has not been tampered with or forged. Second, it validates that the token has not expired by comparing the exp claim against the current timestamp. Third, it verifies the token structure contains required claims (userId, email, username, role, etc.) with proper values.

Security considerations include protecting the signing secret and never exposing it to client code. The operation does not require authentication (members can validate tokens before logging in), but it operates on the same token validation logic used internally by protected endpoints. Invalid tokens receive a detailed response explaining the specific validation failure for debugging purposes.

The response indicates token validity status with specific failure reasons if validation fails. Valid tokens return success confirmation with decoded claims. Expired tokens return a specific error code enabling clients to trigger token refresh via the refresh endpoint. Tampered or malformed tokens return security warnings. The operation is stateless and does not depend on session database lookups for basic cryptographic validation.

This operation integrates with the JWT token system defined in user authentication requirements. It supports the client-side token validation workflow where SDKs check token validity before making requests, improving performance by avoiding unnecessary failed API calls and enabling proactive token refresh.

operations.summary: Validate a moderator's authentication token and active session
operations.description:
This operation validates that a moderator's authentication token is still valid and their associated session remains active. The operation requires the moderator to include their current access token in the Authorization header (Bearer token format).

Validation Process: The system performs the following checks on the provided token: (1) Verifies the token signature using the configured signing secret, (2) Checks that the token has not expired by comparing the exp claim against current time, (3) Extracts the moderator ID from the token claims, (4) Queries the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table to confirm an active session exists for that moderator, (5) Verifies the session's expired_at field is null (indicating an active, non-terminated session), (6) Confirms the moderator's account_status in discussion_board_moderators table is 'active'.

Token Structure: The access token contains JWT claims including userId (moderator ID), email, username, displayName, role ('moderator'), emailVerified status, issued-at timestamp (iat), and expiration timestamp (exp). The token is signed using HS256 algorithm with a secure secret key.

Session Management: Sessions represent individual logins and can persist across multiple API requests. A moderator can have multiple concurrent sessions (e.g., logged in from different devices). Each session has a unique ID and tracks the IP address, URL, and referrer from which the session originated. Sessions are marked expired after 7 days of creation or when explicitly terminated via DELETE /auth/moderator/sessions/{sessionId}.

Error Handling: If the token is invalid, expired, or the corresponding session is inactive, the operation returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized. If the moderator account has been suspended or terminated (account_status != 'active'), the operation denies validation even if the token appears valid. This ensures immediate revocation of access when a moderator role is removed.

Use Cases: This operation is typically called by the client periodically or when accessing protected resources to determine if session refresh is needed. If validation fails, the client knows to request a new token using the refresh token endpoint or prompt the moderator to log in again.

operations.description:
Issue a formal warning to a member account due to policy violations or community guideline breaches. This operation documents moderator-initiated disciplinary action without immediately restricting member access, serving as a first escalation step before potential account suspension.

The warning action is recorded in the discussion_board_user_warnings table with action_type of 'warning', capturing the moderator identity, warning reason, and optional detailed notes. The operation maintains an immutable audit trail of all disciplinary actions for accountability and consistency review. Warnings accumulate in a member's moderation history, allowing moderators to review escalation patterns and understand the context for more severe actions like suspension or termination.

When a warning is issued, the system SHALL send a notification email to the warned member's registered email address explaining the policy violation, the specific reason for the warning, and what behavior changes are expected. The email includes information about potential consequences of continued violations (suspension, then termination). Members can view their warning history in their account settings to understand their moderation status.

When a moderator issues a warning, they must provide a business reason (10-500 characters) explaining the violation category or specific problematic behavior. Optional moderator notes (up to 1000 characters) allow detailed context-setting for other moderators reviewing this member's history, such as references to previous violations, specific comments/articles that triggered the warning, or escalation justification.

Warnings persist indefinitely in the member's moderation history and do not auto-expire. They serve as permanent record of disciplinary actions, enabling moderators to track patterns across extended timeframes. The warning does not automatically restrict member posting rights—members continue to participate normally. However, repeated warnings form the basis for escalation to suspension or termination actions.

This operation is exclusively available to moderator accounts. Only users with moderator role can issue warnings through this endpoint. Member accounts attempting to access this endpoint receive HTTP 403 Forbidden response.

operations.description:
Temporarily suspend a member account due to repeated or severe policy violations, preventing article creation and comment posting while preserving viewing access. This operation escalates account restrictions beyond warnings when members continue violating community guidelines despite previous warnings or commit serious single violations.

The suspension action is recorded in the discussion_board_user_warnings table with action_type of 'suspension', capturing the moderator identity, suspension reason, suspension end date (for automatic reactivation), and optional moderator notes. The operation also updates the member's account_status field in discussion_board_members to 'suspended', which triggers business logic to prevent login and restrict posting privileges system-wide.

When a member account is suspended, the system SHALL:
- Prevent the suspended member from logging into their account
- Prevent the suspended member from creating new articles
- Prevent the suspended member from posting new comments
- Allow the suspended member to view published articles and comments (read-only access)
- Allow the suspended member to view their own unpublished/rejected articles
- Send a notification email to the suspended member's registered email address explaining the suspension reason, exact suspension end date/time (in UTC), and instructions for what to do

The moderator must provide a business reason for suspension (10-500 characters) selecting from predefined categories or custom text. Predefined categories include: 'Repeated Violations', 'Harassment', 'Spam', 'Hate Speech', 'Copyright Violation', or 'Other'. Optional moderator notes (up to 1000 characters) provide internal documentation of the suspension rationale for other moderators' reference.

The moderator must specify the suspension duration through the suspension_end_date parameter. Suspension periods typically range from 7 days to 30 days for temporary suspensions. The suspension_end_date must be a future timestamp in UTC format. The system automatically reactivates the account at the specified date/time, updating account_status back to 'active' and sending a notification to the member that their suspension has expired.

Temporary suspensions are designed as graduated enforcement tool—they restrict posting privileges while preserving account data and allowing eventual return to participation. The automatic reactivation mechanism removes administrative burden of manual account restoration. If a member violates guidelines again after suspension ends, moderators can issue another suspension or escalate to permanent termination.

This operation is exclusively available to moderator accounts. Only users with moderator role can suspend member accounts through this endpoint. Member accounts or guests attempting to access this endpoint receive HTTP 403 Forbidden response.

operations.summary: Permanently ban a discussion board member account
operations.description:
Permanently ban a member account from the discussion board system. This operation sets the member's account status to 'terminated', preventing them from logging in or accessing any platform features. The ban is permanent and can only be reversed by system administrators through direct database intervention.

The requesting moderator must provide a detailed ban reason explaining why the member's account is being terminated. This reason is recorded in the audit trail and communicated to the banned member via email notification, ensuring transparency in the moderation decision.

Security and authorization: Only moderators can execute this operation, as it represents the most severe account restriction available. The operation validates that the requesting user has moderator privileges before proceeding. Banning a member account is a significant action and requires careful consideration of the member's behavior history and violation severity.

Business logic and effects: When a member is banned, their account becomes completely inaccessible. The member cannot log in with their credentials, cannot create new articles or comments, and their previously published content remains visible on the platform but is attributed to a deleted/banned user account. The ban timestamp is recorded in the deleted_at field for audit purposes.

Create a new system configuration setting or update an existing setting in the discussion_board_system_settings table to control platform behavior and features.

System settings are key-value configuration pairs that store application configuration, feature flags, and operational parameters. Settings include site metadata (site_name, site_description, support_email), feature flags controlling functionality availability (enable_new_user_registrations, enable_comments, enable_file_uploads, enable_search), moderation settings (require_article_approval, auto_moderate_comments, spam_detection_enabled), rate limiting parameters (max_articles_per_day, max_comments_per_day, max_comment_burst), and system behavior controls (maintenance_mode, maintenance_message, session_timeout_minutes).

The setting_key must be unique; attempting to create a setting with a duplicate key should either fail with an appropriate error or update the existing setting depending on implementation design.

The operation automatically records audit trail information including the moderator/administrator ID creating or modifying the setting (updated_by field) and timestamps for creation (created_at) and modification (updated_at). New settings default to active status (is_active = true), meaning they are immediately applied by the system. The immutable design principle means modifications to existing settings create new entries with updated timestamps rather than overwriting previous values, preserving the complete configuration history for audit and compliance purposes.

System settings changes are applied immediately or on the next request depending on setting type and system architecture. Some settings (like maintenance_mode or feature flags) may require cache invalidation or application state refresh to take effect. The is_active flag allows administrators to disable specific settings without deleting their configuration history, supporting both temporary feature disabling and permanent configuration removal by marking as inactive.

Related operations: GET /systemSettings/{settingKey} retrieves a specific setting by its key. PATCH /systemSettings with filtering enables retrieving multiple settings efficiently or searching settings by various criteria. The created setting can be modified by calling this POST operation again with the same setting_key to create an updated entry (following immutable design), or via a PUT operation if direct update endpoints are available.

Update an existing system setting that controls application behavior and configuration.

This operation allows moderators and administrators to modify system-wide settings that govern platform functionality, feature availability, rate limits, and operational behavior. The setting_key parameter uniquely identifies which configuration parameter to update (e.g., 'maintenance_mode', 'max_articles_per_day', 'site_name', 'enable_user_registrations'). Each setting consists of a value (the actual configuration), type (string, integer, boolean, or json), and active status (whether the setting is currently applied by the system).

The operation validates that the provided setting_key exists in the system_settings table before processing the update. The update modifies the setting_value field to the new configuration value, updates the setting_type to indicate the data format, changes the is_active flag to control whether the setting is applied, records the update timestamp (updated_at), and captures the administrator identity who made the change (updated_by) for audit trail purposes.

System settings are immutable in the sense that modifications create historical records rather than overwriting previous values completely. The updated_at timestamp marks when this particular configuration version was last modified. The is_active field controls whether the setting is currently applied—inactive settings are stored but ignored by the application, allowing administrators to disable specific settings without losing configuration history.

Common settings that can be modified include site metadata (site_name, site_description, support_email), feature flags (enable_new_user_registrations, enable_comments, enable_file_uploads, enable_search), moderation settings (require_article_approval, auto_moderate_comments, spam_detection_enabled), rate limiting parameters (max_articles_per_day, max_comments_per_day, max_comment_burst), and system behavior controls (maintenance_mode, maintenance_message, session_timeout_minutes).

The operation requires moderator or administrator authorization to ensure that only authorized personnel can modify system configuration. Changes to system settings take effect immediately or on the next request depending on the setting type and system design. This centralized configuration management eliminates the need to modify environment variables or restart the application for routine configuration changes.

operations.description:
Permanently remove a system setting from the configuration database.

This operation allows moderators and administrators to delete system-wide settings that are no longer needed or have become obsolete. The setting_key parameter uniquely identifies which configuration parameter to delete (e.g., 'maintenance_mode', 'max_articles_per_day', 'site_name'). Once deleted, the setting is completely removed from the system_settings table and is no longer available for the application to retrieve or use.

The operation validates that the provided setting_key exists in the system_settings table before processing the deletion. Upon successful deletion, the setting is permanently removed from the database. This is a hard delete operation with no recovery mechanism—the deleted setting entry cannot be restored by regular users and is only preserved in database backups or administrative recovery procedures.

Deletion of system settings should be performed carefully, as removing an active setting may cause the application to lose important configuration values or fall back to default behaviors. For example, deleting 'maintenance_mode' removes the maintenance mode configuration, potentially affecting system availability management. Deleting 'max_articles_per_day' removes the rate limiting configuration, affecting spam prevention.

System settings that control critical functionality (such as authentication settings, security parameters, or core feature flags) should typically be deactivated (is_active set to false) rather than deleted, allowing the configuration history to be preserved and the setting to be easily re-enabled if needed.

The operation requires moderator or administrator authorization to ensure that only authorized personnel can delete system configuration. For audit purposes, the system logs the deletion action with the administrator identity and timestamp, maintaining a record of when and by whom the setting was removed, even though the setting itself is permanently deleted from the active configuration database.
