IDiscussionBoardMember.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for member registration and account creation. Contains credentials and profile information needed to create a new discussion board account.

The registration process validates all input data according to business rules: email must be unique and in valid RFC 5322 format, username must be unique (case-insensitive) with alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen characters only, and display_name must be 1-50 characters. Password is hashed using bcrypt (minimum 12 rounds) on the backend before storage.

Upon successful registration, the system creates the member account with email_verified set to false, requiring email verification before full posting privileges are granted. The account_status defaults to 'active', created_at is set to current timestamp, and updated_at mirrors created_at. The member cannot create articles or post comments until they verify their email address through the verification link sent to their email.

The registration endpoint typically returns the created member without exposing the password_hash field, confirming the new account creation and prompting the member to verify their email address.

Guest sessions are temporary and tracked through the unique guest identifier. Each guest receives JWT tokens for maintaining their session across API requests. Guest users have restricted permissions preventing content creation, comments, or any write operations on the platform.

The authorization response enables immediate access to the discussion board for unauthenticated visitors to explore content and view discussions without requiring account registration.

IDiscussionBoardMember.ILogin.description:
Member login credentials for authentication. Accepts either email or username as the login identifier, along with the member's password for credential validation.

The operation validates the provided credentials against stored member records in the discussion_board_members table. Authentication succeeds only if the identifier matches an existing member account and the password hash matches the provided password. Upon successful authentication, a new session is created with connection context (IP address, referrer URL) and JWT tokens are issued.

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) capture connection metadata for audit trails and security monitoring. The href field (current page URL) and referrer field (previous page URL) are mandatory for tracking the origin of the login request, while the ip field is optional as server can extract it from the request context.

Business Rule: Either email OR username must be provided for login identification - the schema structure allows both fields but application logic must validate that at least one is supplied.

email.description: Member email address for login identification. Either email or username must be provided - this field is optional if username is supplied. Email matching is case-insensitive. Maximum 254 characters per RFC 5321.

Minimum 8 characters required. Passwords should meet complexity requirements: at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one special character for security best practices.

The operation creates a new record in the discussion_board_moderators table with timestamps created_at and updated_at set to the current time, enabling the newly registered moderator to access moderation features immediately.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.description:
Discussion articles representing the primary content type on the discussion board platform.

Articles are forum discussion threads initiated by members about economic and political topics. Each article flows through a moderation workflow before publication and requires moderator approval before becoming visible to other users. Articles support rich content through text and file attachments.

Articles form the foundation of community discussion and represent the primary business entities that users create to initiate conversations. The article lifecycle includes submission, moderator review, approval/rejection/request for changes, and optional publication. Published articles accumulate comments from community members, creating threaded discussions.

Each article maintains a persistent record including creator attribution, category classification, publication status, and engagement metrics. Articles support the complete content discovery workflow through search, category filtering, and member navigation.

Note: Comments are retrieved via the dedicated GET /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/comments endpoint with pagination support, not embedded in the article response. This design pattern optimizes payload size and follows REST API best practices for nested resources.

The status determines visibility permissions (who can see the article) and editing permissions (whether the creator can make changes). Different API endpoints may filter based on user role and article status to enforce appropriate access control.

published_at.description:
Timestamp when article status changed to published (moderator approval). Null if article is not yet published, was rejected, or archived. Records the official publication moment for audit purposes.

For published articles, indicates the approval time showing when the content became publicly visible to all users. Enables sorting by publication date and understanding the approval timeline. Essential for displaying publication context in article views.

rejection_reason.description:
Text explanation provided by moderator when article is rejected. Helps article creator understand why content did not meet guidelines and what improvements are needed for resubmission. Maximum 500 characters.

Null if article has not been rejected. When an article is rejected, this field contains the moderator's feedback explaining the reason and guidance for resubmission. Critical for rejected articles to show context and help authors improve their content before resubmission.

creator.description: The member who created and authored this article. Provides author attribution displayed with the article in list views. Includes creator's display name, status, and account information for identifying article source.

category.description: The category this article belongs to (Economics, Politics, Economic Policy, Political Analysis, Other). Provides topic classification for list display. Enables users to understand article subject matter and browse by category.

comments_count.description: Count of non-deleted comments on this article. Provides engagement metrics in list views to show discussion activity and community participation level. Excludes soft-deleted comments from the count.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary.description:
Lightweight article summary for efficient list views and search results.

Provides essential article information needed for display in article lists, search results, category browsing, and moderation queues. Summary variants are optimized for efficient transmission in paginated lists with reduced payload size.

Includes primary identifiers, core content fields, engagement metrics (view count, comments count), author and category references, and optional metadata fields (published_at for approval context, rejection_reason for rejected articles). Notably excludes full article body content to reduce payload size for list operations. Clients requiring the complete article content should use the GET detail endpoint (GET /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}).

The summary structure balances information completeness for list displays with payload efficiency for high-volume pagination scenarios. Article body is not included in this view as full content is typically unnecessary for discovery and browsing operations.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest.description:
Search criteria for querying articles and comments across the discussion board platform.

This request DTO enables comprehensive search functionality allowing members to discover relevant discussions and comments. The search supports full-text matching across article titles, article bodies, and comment content using GIN indexes for optimized text matching.

Search parameters include keywords, filters by category, article status (published/pending/rejected), member author, date ranges, and pagination controls. Results can be sorted by relevance (default), chronological order (newest/oldest), or engagement metrics such as view count and comment count.

The search feature enables content discovery, allowing members to find existing discussions before creating new articles and to follow conversations of interest. Search results respect visibility rules—only published articles and non-deleted comments are returned.

q.description: Search keyword or query string for full-text matching. Searches across article titles, article bodies, and comment content using GIN indexes. Minimum 1 character, maximum 500 characters. Required for search operation.

categories.description: Optional array of category UUIDs to filter search results. Only articles belonging to these categories are included in results. If empty or omitted, all categories are included in search. References discussion_board_categories.id.

status.description: Optional array of article statuses to filter results. Valid values: 'pending_approval', 'published', 'rejected', 'archived'. If omitted, defaults to ['published'] for regular members. Administrators may search across multiple statuses. Respects member permissions—rejected articles only visible to creator and moderators.

member_id.description: Optional member UUID to filter results by article author or comment author. When provided, only articles and comments created by this member are returned. References discussion_board_members.id. Null or omitted includes all members.

date_from.description: Optional ISO 8601 datetime for filtering results created on or after this timestamp. Null or omitted includes all dates. Used to narrow search to recent content.

date_to.description: Optional ISO 8601 datetime for filtering results created on or before this timestamp. Null or omitted includes all dates. Used to limit search to older content or specific date ranges.

oneOf.description: Sort order for search results. Values: 'relevance' (default, full-text match score), 'newest' (most recent articles/comments first), 'oldest' (oldest first), 'view_count' (most viewed articles first), 'comment_count' (articles with most comments first).

page.description: Page number for pagination, starting from 1. Each page contains up to 'limit' results. Default: 1.

include_comments.description: Whether to include comments in search results. If true, both articles and comments matching the search criteria are returned. If false, only articles are returned. Default: true.

deleted_only.description: If true, search includes soft-deleted articles (deleted_at is not null). If false, only non-deleted articles are included. Used primarily by moderators for content recovery. Default: false.

email.description: Member's email address used for authentication, password recovery, and communication. Must be unique across all members and valid email format (maximum 254 characters). Verified before member gains full posting privileges.

username.description: Member's chosen username for login and public identification. Case-insensitive with unique constraint. 3-30 characters, alphanumeric plus underscore and hyphen. Used as alternative login identifier and displayed in search results.

display_name.description: Public-facing display name shown as author attribution on articles and comments. 1-50 characters. May differ from username for privacy or professional presentation. Shows to all users viewing the member's content.

email_verified.description: Flag indicating whether member's email address has been verified. False for new registrations before email verification. Must be true before member can create articles or post comments. Set to true when member clicks verification link sent to their email.

IDiscussionBoardMember.description:

Members authenticate via email/username and password, undergo email verification before gaining full posting access, and can be suspended or deleted. Each member maintains a persistent audit trail of their activities and moderation history.

The member entity forms the foundation of the discussion community, enabling user management, authentication, and accountability for content. Members create both articles (discussion threads) and comments (responses), making them the primary actors in the system.

Account status and email verification control access permissions. Soft deletion enables account recovery while maintaining data integrity for audit purposes.

IDiscussionBoardMember.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a member for reference in articles and comments.

Includes only the essential identification information needed when displaying member involvement in content creation. Used when showing article authors and comment creators without exposing email, authentication details, or account history. Efficient for list views and embedding in other entities.

id.description: Unique identifier for the category. System-generated UUID primary key used to reference this category from articles and API responses.

name.description: Display name of the category shown to users. Examples: 'Economics', 'Politics', 'Economic Policy'. Maximum 50 characters for consistent display in UI.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier for the category used in filtering, search, and API endpoints. Examples: 'economics', 'political-analysis'. Lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens only. Must be unique across all categories.

description.description: Detailed description of the category's purpose and scope. Explains what types of discussions belong here. Displayed to users when browsing or creating articles. Maximum 500 characters. Can be null if no description is provided.

display_order.description: Integer sequence number determining category display order in navigation menus. Lower numbers appear first. Categories are sorted by this field for consistent UI presentation. Typical values: 1 (Economics), 2 (Politics), 3 (Economic Policy), 4 (Political Analysis), 5 (Other).

is_active.description: Whether this category is currently available for article selection. Active categories appear in the category filter dropdown and navigation. Inactive categories hide from member selections but retain existing articles. Allows administrators to retire unused categories without data loss.

article_count.description: Denormalized count of published articles currently in this category. Provides quick access for display purposes (e.g., 'Economics (42 articles)'). Automatically updated when articles are published or archived. Initialized to 0 when category is created.

created_at.description: Timestamp when category was created. Records the initial creation time of the category in UTC timezone. Immutable after creation.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to category properties. Updated whenever category name, description, display order, or active status changes. Supports audit trail and change tracking.

IDiscussionBoardCategory.description:
Discussion board categories representing the predefined article classification system.

Categories organize and structure all discussions on the platform by topic area (Economics, Politics, Economic Policy, Political Analysis, Other). They form the foundational reference data maintained by system administrators, enabling users to browse and discover discussions by topic.

Each category tracks the number of published articles for display purposes and maintains active/inactive status to manage category availability. Categories are essential infrastructure supporting article organization and member navigation throughout the discussion board.

Categories provide consistent organization structure, allowing members to filter articles by topic and moderators to manage content categories. While not directly transactional, categories are referenced by all articles and form the backbone of content discovery workflows.

id.description: Unique identifier for the category. System-generated UUID primary key used to reference this category from articles and API responses.

name.description: Display name of the category shown to users. Examples: 'Economics', 'Politics', 'Economic Policy'. Maximum 50 characters for consistent display in UI.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier for the category used in filtering, search, and API endpoints. Examples: 'economics', 'political-analysis'. Lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens only. Must be unique across all categories.

Categories are sorted by this field for consistent UI presentation. Typical values: 1 (Economics), 2 (Politics), 3 (Economic Policy), 4 (Political Analysis), 5 (Other).

article_count.description: Denormalized count of published articles currently in this category. Provides quick access for display purposes (e.g., 'Economics (42 articles)'). Automatically updated when articles are published or archived. Initialized to 0 when category is created.

IDiscussionBoardCategory.ISummary.description:
Lightweight category summary for efficient list views and category navigation.

Provides essential category information needed for display in dropdowns, filters, and navigation menus. Summary variants are optimized for efficient transmission in paginated lists and embedded references.

Includes the primary category identifier, name, and article count for UI display. Excludes detailed descriptions and audit timestamps to reduce payload size for list operations.

title.description: Article title for the discussion topic. Must be between 5 and 200 characters. Provides a clear, concise summary of the discussion subject matter.

body.description: Main article content containing the discussion text. Must be between 10 and 50,000 characters. Contains the detailed discussion content, arguments, analysis, or information related to the discussion topic.

category_id.description: Unique identifier of the category this article belongs to. Must reference an existing category from the discussion_board_categories table. Categories include Economics, Politics, Economic Policy, Political Analysis, and Other for organizing discussions by topic.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new discussion board article.

Article creation requires three essential inputs: a title (5-200 characters), article body content (10-50,000 characters), and selection of an existing category. The authenticated member making the request is automatically assigned as the article creator.

The article is created in pending_approval status, meaning it is not visible to other users until a moderator reviews and approves it. Initial state includes creation timestamp set to current UTC time, view_count initialized to 0, and null values for rejection_reason, published_at, and deleted_at.

This operation requires authentication - only verified members with active accounts can create articles.

title.description: Article title or headline. Must be between 5 and 200 characters. Serves as the primary identifier for discussion topic and appears in article lists and search results.

body.description: Article content body containing the main discussion text. Must be between 10 and 50,000 characters. Supports plain text and basic formatting. This is the core content of the discussion article.

Valid values: pending_approval (submitted but not yet reviewed), published (approved and visible to all users), rejected (did not meet guidelines, visible only to creator and moderators), archived (hidden from public view but retained in system). Determines visibility and editing permissions.

rejection_reason.description: Text explanation provided by moderator when article is rejected. Helps article creator understand why content did not meet guidelines and what improvements are needed for resubmission. Maximum 500 characters. Null to clear rejection reason.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IUpdate.description:
Update request for an existing discussion board article. All fields are optional allowing partial updates. The operation enforces authorization checks to ensure only the article creator or moderators can modify articles.

When an article is updated, the updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed to record the modification time. However, the created_at and published_at timestamps remain immutable and are never modified, preserving the audit trail. Title must remain between 5 and 200 characters, and body content must remain between 10 and 50,000 characters. Category assignments are validated to ensure the referenced category exists. Status updates follow the workflow rules - articles can transition between pending_approval, published, rejected, and archived states based on moderation actions.

id.description: Unique identifier for the comment. System-generated UUID primary key used to reference this comment in API responses and moderation actions.

body.description: Comment text content. Must be between 1 and 5,000 characters. Contains the member's response, perspective, or question about the article. Supports plain text with basic formatting.

is_deleted.description: Soft deletion flag indicating whether comment has been deleted. True if deleted by author or moderator; false if active. Allows recovery of deleted comments for audit purposes while hiding them from user views. Defaults to false.

created_at.description: Timestamp when comment was originally created. Immutable - never changes. Records the exact moment comment was posted for chronological sorting and rate limiting checks.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last edit to comment. Null if comment has never been edited. Updated whenever member modifies comment text or attachments. Allows tracking of comment modifications with edit timestamps displayed to users.

author.description: The member who created this comment. Provides author attribution and member identity context displayed with the comment. Always uses .ISummary to prevent circular references while providing essential author information.

article_id.description: Reference to the parent article this comment belongs to. Used to associate comment with its article and for organizing comments by article.

attachments.description: Array of file and image attachments associated with the comment. Comments can include multiple attachments (images, documents, etc.) uploaded together with the comment content. Attachments are managed as part of the comment composition and are deleted when the comment is deleted.

IDiscussionBoardComment.description:
Comments representing member responses and engagement on published articles.

Comments enable discussion and debate by allowing members to share perspectives, ask questions, and respond to article content. Unlike articles, comments are published immediately without moderation approval, creating immediate visibility and real-time engagement.

Each comment belongs exclusively to one article and extends that article's discussion thread. Comments maintain author information, creation timestamp, attachment references, and support editing for content correction and deletion for content removal with soft deletion preserving comment records for audit purposes.

Comments form the interactive component of the discussion platform, transforming the system from one-way content distribution into collaborative conversation. They represent primary business entities requiring independent management through search, filtering, and moderation capabilities.

Comments are displayed in threaded format under their parent article, enabling members to follow discussion progressions and understand conversational context. Attachments (images and files) provide rich media support for detailed explanations and evidence sharing. Comment counts provide engagement metrics on articles while actual comments are retrieved via dedicated endpoints.

id.description: Unique identifier for the comment. System-generated UUID primary key used to reference this comment in API responses.

body.description: Comment text content. Must be between 1 and 5,000 characters. Contains the member's response, perspective, or question about the article. Supports plain text with basic formatting.

is_deleted.description: Soft deletion flag indicating whether comment has been deleted. True if deleted by author or moderator; false if active. Allows recovery of deleted comments for audit purposes while hiding them from user views.

created_at.description: Timestamp when comment was originally created. Immutable - never changes. Records the exact moment comment was posted for chronological sorting.

author.description: The member who created this comment. Provides author attribution and member identity context. Always uses .ISummary to prevent circular references while providing essential identification information.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ISummary.description:
Lightweight comment summary for efficient display in comment lists and threads.

Provides essential comment information needed for display in threaded comment sections and search results. Summary variants are optimized for efficient transmission in paginated comment lists with reduced payload size compared to full detail views.

Includes comment identifier, content, deletion status, timestamp, and author attribution. Excludes update timestamps, parent article reference, and attachment details to reduce payload size when displayed in threaded comment sections and paginated lists. For full comment details including attachments and edit history, use the full IDiscussionBoardComment response type.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Defaults to 1. Must be positive integer. Pages are 1-indexed (first page is 1).

limit.description: Number of comments to return per page. Defaults to 20. Must be between 1 and 100. Enforces reasonable page size limits to prevent excessive data retrieval.

search.description: Full-text search query to find comments matching the search terms. Searches across comment body content. Optional parameter for content discovery. When provided, returns comments containing matching text.

sortBy.description: Field to sort results by. Valid values: created_at (comment creation date), updated_at (last edit date), author (author display name). Defaults to created_at.

order.description: Sort order direction. Valid values: asc (ascending/oldest first), desc (descending/newest first). Defaults to desc for reverse chronological sorting.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest.description:
Search criteria, filtering options, pagination parameters, and sorting configuration for comment retrieval.

Supports pagination through page and limit parameters. Allows sorting comments by creation date, modification date, or author name. Optional full-text search enables content discovery across comment body content. Sorting and filtering are applied before pagination to ensure accurate result sets.

All parameters are optional and have sensible defaults (page: 1, limit: 20, sortBy: created_at, order: desc). Use these parameters to implement client-side filtering, searching, and pagination controls.

body.description: Comment text content containing the member's response, perspective, or question about the article. Must be between 1 and 5,000 characters. Supports plain text with basic formatting.

attachments.description: Optional array of attachment UUIDs to associate with the comment. References pre-uploaded attachments from the discussion_board_attachments table. Each UUID must reference a valid existing attachment. Maximum 50 attachments per comment. If omitted or empty, comment is created without attachments.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL where comment was created). Used for tracking the context of comment creation. Required field for session tracking and analytics. Recorded in session metadata for audit purposes.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL). Indicates which page referred the member to the comment creation page. Used for tracking user navigation and access patterns. Required field for session context.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new comment on a discussion board article.

Contains the comment text, optional file/image attachment associations, and session context information. The parent article is identified via the {articleId} path parameter—never provided in the request body. The creating member's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token—never provided in the request body.

Comments are published immediately upon creation without requiring moderator approval, creating immediate visibility for community engagement. The comment body must be between 1 and 5,000 characters of plain text with basic formatting. Attachments (if included) must be pre-uploaded to the storage system and referenced by their UUID.

Session context fields (href, referrer) are required for tracking the connection context and user navigation patterns when comment was created. These fields enable session management and audit trail capabilities.

No id, created_at, updated_at, discussion_board_article_id, or is_deleted fields are included—these are managed by the system. The article ID is provided via the path parameter {articleId}, and the discussion_board_member_id (author) is populated automatically from the authenticated JWT token.

id.description: Unique identifier of the attachment. Used to identify and access this specific file or image within the discussion board system.

parent_type.description: Type of parent content this attachment belongs to. Either 'article' (references discussion_board_articles) or 'comment' (references discussion_board_comments). Enables polymorphic relationship without multiple nullable foreign keys.

parent_id.description: UUID of the parent content (article or comment) this attachment is associated with. Combined with parent_type to identify the parent entity.

original_filename.description: Original filename as uploaded by the user (max 255 characters). Used for display in UI and download dialog. May contain spaces and special characters.

storage_path.description: System-generated file path where attachment is stored. Uses secure naming pattern (timestamp_hash_originalname) to prevent directory traversal attacks. Unique across entire system.

file_size.description: File size in bytes. Validated at upload time to ensure limits are enforced (10 MB for images, 25 MB for documents). Used for quota tracking and display to users.

mime_type.description: MIME type of the file (e.g., image/jpeg, application/pdf, text/plain). Determined by magic number verification (file header inspection) not file extension, for security.

file_hash.description: SHA-256 hash of file content for integrity verification and malware scanning. Computed at upload time and used to detect file corruption or tampering.

is_image.description: Whether this attachment is an image file. Used to determine display method (embedded inline for images, downloadable link for documents) and whether image dimensions are captured.

oneOf.description: Image width in pixels (for image attachments only). Used for display sizing and validation (must be 100-8000 pixels).
Null for non-image files.

width.description: Image width in pixels for image attachments, or null for non-image files. Represents the horizontal dimension of the image used for display sizing and aspect ratio preservation. Only populated for files where is_image is true; null for document attachments.

oneOf.description: Image height in pixels (for image attachments only). Used for display sizing and aspect ratio preservation.
Null for non-image files.

height.description: Image height in pixels for image attachments, or null for non-image files. Represents the vertical dimension of the image used for display sizing and aspect ratio preservation. Only populated for files where is_image is true; null for document attachments.

created_at.description: Timestamp when attachment was uploaded. Immutable after creation. Used for audit trails and display of upload time to users.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last modification. Updated when attachment metadata is modified. Usually equals created_at except when file is replaced or metadata edited.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when attachment was soft-deleted. Records when the attachment was removed from active use.
Null if attachment is active.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp indicating when the attachment was deleted, or null if the attachment is currently active. Enables audit trail preservation and recovery within the retention window. When populated, the attachment is hidden from user views but remains in the database for compliance purposes.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.description:
File and image attachment associated with articles and comments on the discussion board.

Represents a single file or image attachment that is linked to either an article or comment through a polymorphic relationship. Stores complete metadata about the uploaded file including its original name, secure storage location, file size, MIME type, and integrity hash.

Attachments support multiple file types including images (JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP with 10 MB limit) and documents (PDF, DOCX, TXT, XLS, XLSX, CSV, ODT, ODS, ODP, ZIP with 25 MB limit). Image files automatically have their dimensions captured and stored for proper display rendering.

Each attachment maintains audit trails through creation and modification timestamps, with soft deletion support preserving records for compliance and recovery purposes. When parent content is deleted, associated attachments are automatically removed from the system.

parent_type.description:
Type of parent content this attachment belongs to. Fixed constant value 'comment' for comment attachments.

Enables polymorphic relationship identification in the database.

parent_id.description:
UUID of the parent comment this attachment is associated with. Required to establish the relationship between attachment and comment.

Must reference an existing discussion_board_comments record.

original_filename.description:
Original filename of the attachment. Must be a non-empty string up to 255 characters preserving the user's intended filename.

Used for display in UI and download dialogs.

mime_type.description: MIME type of the attachment (e.g., image/jpeg, application/pdf, text/plain). Should be verified for security before accepting. Only supported file types allowed (images: JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP; documents: PDF, DOCX, TXT, XLS, XLSX, CSV, ODT, ODS, ODP, ZIP).

file_size.description:
Size of the attachment file in bytes. Must be non-negative and within system limits: 10 MB (10485760 bytes) for images, 25 MB (26214400 bytes) for documents.

Validation occurs at upload time to enforce these constraints.

storage_path.description: System-generated secure storage path for the file. References the location where the file is stored (e.g., S3 bucket path, CDN location). Uses secure naming pattern (timestamp_hash_originalname) to prevent directory traversal attacks.

file_hash.description: SHA-256 hash of the file content for integrity verification and malware scanning. Provided by the client or calculated by the system to ensure file authenticity and detect tampering.

is_image.description:
Whether this attachment is an image file. Used to determine display method (embedded inline for images, downloadable link for documents) and whether image dimensions should be captured.

Required to properly classify attachment type for storage and display logic.

width.description:
Image width in pixels (for image attachments only). Null for non-image files. When provided, must be between 100-8000 pixels for validation.

Optional field populated only when the attachment is an image file.

height.description:
Image height in pixels (for image attachments only). Null for non-image files. When provided, must be between 100-8000 pixels for validation.

Optional field populated only when the attachment is an image file.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating attachment records associated with comments. Contains complete attachment metadata including parent relationship identification, filename, MIME type, file size, storage path, SHA-256 hash for integrity verification, and image dimensions (for image files).

Enables atomic creation of attachment-comment relationships by providing full context including parent comment identification. All file attachments must be pre-uploaded to storage before creating attachment records via this DTO.

Supports polymorphic attachment handling with parent_type and parent_id fields enabling reuse for article attachments as well.

body.description:
The updated text content of the comment. Must be a non-empty string between 1 and 5,000 characters representing the member's comment or response on the article.

Text content is validated for length constraints and required for comment updates. The body contains plain text with basic formatting support for member responses, perspectives, and questions about article content.

Note: Attachments associated with comments are managed separately through dedicated API endpoints (POST /articles/{articleId}/attachments for adding, DELETE /articles/{articleId}/attachments/{attachmentId} for removing). Attachment lifecycle is independent of comment updates and should not be modified through this DTO.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IUpdate.description:
Update request for an existing discussion board comment. Contains the modified comment content for updating a comment's text body while preserving the original creation timestamp and author information.

This DTO is used when a member or moderator updates a comment's text body. The operation validates ownership or moderator status before allowing the update and maintains an audit trail by updating the system-managed updated_at timestamp.

Attachment management is handled separately through dedicated endpoints and is NOT included in comment update operations. This separation maintains clear boundaries for atomic operations and allows independent management of attachments across the system.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-indexed). Specifies which page of results to retrieve when searching attachments. Used in conjunction with limit to enable efficient pagination through large attachment result sets.

limit.description: Number of attachment records to return per page. Limited to a maximum of 100 items for performance optimization. Defaults to reasonable page size when not specified to balance between data transfer and query efficiency.

search.description: Search query for filtering attachments by original filename. Supports partial matching to find attachments by name pattern, enabling users to locate files by name without requiring exact matches.

file_type.description: MIME type filter to search for attachments by file type. Examples: 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf', 'text/plain'. Enables filtering for specific file categories and document types.

min_size.description: Minimum file size in bytes for filtering attachments. Returns only attachments larger than or equal to this size, enabling filtering by file size constraints.

max_size.description: Maximum file size in bytes for filtering attachments. Returns only attachments smaller than or equal to this size, enabling filtering by maximum file size limits.

upload_date_from.description: Filter attachments uploaded on or after this date (ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD). Supports date range filtering for attachment uploads to find files by upload timeframe.

upload_date_to.description: Filter attachments uploaded on or before this date (ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD). Combined with upload_date_from for date range queries to filter attachments by upload period.

include_deleted.description: Include soft-deleted attachments in the search results. When true, shows attachments marked as deleted; when false (default), only returns active attachments. Primarily used for moderator and admin views for auditing purposes.

oneOf.description: Sort results by attachment creation/upload date
Sort results by original filename
Sort results by file size in bytes
Sort results by MIME type

sort_by.description: Field to sort attachment results by. Options include created_at (upload date), filename (original name), file_size (bytes), or file_type (MIME type). Determines the primary sort order for returned attachments.

oneOf.description: Ascending order (smallest to largest, A to Z)
Descending order (largest to smallest, Z to A)

sort_order.description: Sort direction - ascending (asc) or descending (desc). Controls whether results are ordered from smallest to largest or vice versa based on the sort_by field selection.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for querying discussion board attachments. Enables complex read-only queries to find attachments based on filename, file type, size range, upload date range, and deletion status.

Supports pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options on various attachment metadata fields including creation date, filename, file size, and MIME type. All filter parameters are optional, enabling flexible query construction from strict filtering to broad searches.

Used exclusively with PATCH operations to retrieve filtered lists of attachments associated with articles. This is a read-only query DTO and does not support write operations - attachment creation and deletion use separate dedicated endpoints.

id.description: Unique identifier for the attachment. Used to reference this attachment in API operations and download requests.

oneOf.description:
Type of parent content this attachment belongs to. Either 'article' (references discussion_board_articles) or 'comment' (references discussion_board_comments).

Enables polymorphic relationship identification without requiring multiple nullable foreign keys. Critical for understanding whether this attachment is part of an article or comment.

Type of parent content this attachment belongs to. Either 'article' (references discussion_board_articles) or 'comment' (references discussion_board_comments).

Enables polymorphic relationship identification without requiring multiple nullable foreign keys. Critical for understanding whether this attachment is part of an article or comment.

parent_type.description:
Type of parent content this attachment belongs to. Either 'article' (references discussion_board_articles) or 'comment' (references discussion_board_comments).

Enables polymorphic relationship identification without requiring multiple nullable foreign keys. Critical for understanding whether this attachment is part of an article or comment.

parent_id.description:
UUID of the parent content (article or comment) this attachment is associated with. Combined with parent_type to uniquely identify the parent entity.

Allows clients to navigate from attachment back to its containing article or comment for context and operations.

original_filename.description:
Original filename as uploaded by the user (maximum 255 characters). Used for display in UI and download dialog. May contain spaces and special characters for user readability.

Provides the name users see when downloading or previewing the attachment.

mime_type.description:
MIME type of the file (e.g., image/jpeg, application/pdf, text/plain). Determined by magic number verification (file header inspection) not file extension, for security and accuracy.

Used to determine appropriate display method (embedded inline for images, downloadable link for documents) and client-side handling.

file_size.description:
File size in bytes. Validated at upload time to ensure limits are enforced (10 MB for images, 25 MB for documents). Used for quota tracking, storage planning, and user information about file size before download.

Provides transparency to users about file size and helps with bandwidth planning.

is_image.description:
Whether this attachment is an image file. Used to determine display method (embedded inline for images, downloadable link for documents) and whether image dimensions are captured and displayed.

Allows clients to render images inline versus rendering document download links.

width.description:
Image width in pixels (for image attachments only). Null for non-image files. Used for display sizing and validation that images are within acceptable dimension ranges (100-8000 pixels).

Allows clients to properly size and display images in UI layouts.

height.description:
Image height in pixels (for image attachments only). Null for non-image files. Used for display sizing and aspect ratio preservation in UI rendering.

Allows clients to calculate aspect ratios and maintain proper image display proportions.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when attachment was uploaded in ISO 8601 format. Immutable after creation. Used for audit trails, display of upload time to users, and chronological sorting of attachments.

Records when the file was originally uploaded to the system.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of last modification in ISO 8601 format. Updated when attachment metadata is modified. Usually equals created_at except when file is replaced or metadata edited.

Tracks when the attachment record was last changed in the system.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when attachment was soft-deleted in ISO 8601 format. Null if attachment is active. Soft deletion preserves attachment record for audit purposes while hiding from user views.

Used to identify deleted attachments and maintain historical audit trails without permanently removing data.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a file or image attachment for display in article and comment contexts.

Provides essential attachment metadata including filename, file type, size, and image dimensions (if applicable). This lightweight summary is used when attachments are displayed within articles or comments, providing users with information about attached files without loading full attachment details.

Includes complete parent context identification, file identification, size information for user awareness, and image dimensions for proper rendering. Used in attachment listings and embedded attachment previews within content contexts.

name.description:
Display name of the category shown to users for organizational and navigation purposes.

Examples: 'Economics', 'Politics', 'Economic Policy'. Maximum 50 characters for consistent display in UI. Must be unique across all categories to prevent duplicate category names and maintain clear organizational structure.

oneOf.description: Detailed description of the category's purpose and scope. Explains what types of discussions belong in this category to help users understand when to use it.
No description provided for this category. Null value indicates the category operates without additional contextual information.

description.description:
Detailed description of the category explaining its purpose, scope, and what types of articles belong in this category.

Optional field (can be null) that provides additional context for users. Maximum 500 characters when provided. Displayed to users when browsing or creating articles to clarify category usage.

slug.description:
URL-safe identifier for the category used in filtering, search, and API endpoints.

Examples: 'economics', 'political-analysis'. Lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens only. Must be unique across all categories to ensure consistent API references and bookmarkable URLs.

display_order.description:
Integer sequence number determining category display order in navigation menus and category lists.

Lower numbers appear first. Categories are sorted by this field for consistent UI presentation across the platform. Typical values: 1 (Economics), 2 (Politics), 3 (Economic Policy), 4 (Political Analysis), 5 (Other). Can be adjusted when reorganizing category hierarchy.

is_active.description:
Whether this category is currently available for article selection by members.

Active categories appear in the category filter dropdown and navigation menus. Inactive categories are hidden from member selections but retain all existing articles for historical purposes. Allows administrators to retire unused categories without data loss or breaking article references.

IDiscussionBoardCategory.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new discussion board article category.

Required fields specify the category name, URL slug, display order, and active status. The name and slug must be unique across the system to prevent duplicate categories and maintain clear organizational structure. Optional description provides additional category details for improved organization and presentation to users.

All provided values are validated for uniqueness (name and slug), format compliance (slug must be URL-safe), and adherence to platform naming conventions and character limits. Category creation is restricted to moderators and administrators with appropriate permissions. The creator's identity is automatically captured from the authentication context.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Defaults to 1 if not specified

limit.description: Number of categories to return per page. Maximum is 100. Defaults to 20 if not specified

search.description: Optional search query to filter categories by name or description containing the search term

oneOf.description: Sort by category name alphabetically
Sort by category creation date
Sort by display order (default)

order_by.description: Field to sort categories by. Options are: name (alphabetical), created_at (creation date), display_order (display order). Defaults to display_order if not specified

oneOf.description: Sort in ascending order
Sort in descending order

direction.description: Sort direction. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Defaults to 'asc' if not specified

oneOf.description: Filter by category active status
No active status filter applied

is_active.description: Optional filter by active status. If specified, returns only categories with matching active state. If null or omitted, returns all categories

IDiscussionBoardCategory.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for searching and filtering discussion board categories.

Supports pagination with configurable page size, full-text search across category name and description, and sorting by multiple fields. Filtering by active status allows retrieval of only available categories or all categories including inactive ones.

All parameters are optional and default to sensible values for general category browsing. Pagination is required for efficient large dataset retrieval.

name.description: Display name of the category shown to users. When provided in an update request, allows renaming an existing category to reflect organizational changes. Must remain unique across all categories.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier for the category used in filtering, search, and API endpoints. When provided, allows updating the category's URL-safe reference identifier. Must remain unique across all categories to maintain consistent API references.

oneOf.description: Detailed description of the category explaining its purpose and scope
Null value to clear the category description

description.description: Detailed description of the category's purpose and scope. Optional in update requests - can be set to null to remove the description. Maximum 500 characters when provided.

display_order.description: Integer sequence number determining category display order in navigation menus. When provided, updates the position of this category relative to others. Lower numbers appear first.

is_active.description: Whether this category is currently available for article selection. When updated to false, the category is hidden from member UI but retains all existing articles. Updated to true reactivates a previously inactive category.

IDiscussionBoardCategory.IUpdate.description:
Update request for an existing discussion board article category.

All fields are optional in update requests, allowing partial updates of category properties. Provide only the fields you wish to modify; omitted fields retain their current values. Useful for updating category name, description, display order, or active status independently.

Validation applies to updated values: name and slug must remain unique, slug must be URL-safe, and values must conform to character limits. Update operations are restricted to moderators and administrators with appropriate permissions. The update timestamp is automatically recorded.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for retrieving a paginated list of discussion board members.

This request DTO enables member discovery and listing functionality supporting both regular members browsing the community and administrators managing member accounts. Supports filtering members by account status (active, suspended, terminated, deleted), email verification status, and search capabilities by username or display name for targeted member discovery.

Pagination parameters control result set size and offset for efficient client-side rendering of large member lists. Sorting options allow ordering by membership duration (created_at), display name, last login activity, article contribution count, or other engagement metrics. All filter and sort parameters are optional, enabling flexible query composition from simple searches to complex multi-criteria filtering.

The operation respects member privacy settings and returns only publicly-visible member information. Security enforces that only verified active members are visible in public member lists by default, while suspended or terminated accounts are excluded from public discovery. Personal information such as email addresses are never included in results.

search.description:
Optional search query string to filter members by username or display name. Performs case-insensitive substring matching against both fields. When provided, only members whose username or display_name contains the search string are returned.

Null or omitted returns all members without search filtering. Minimum 1 character when provided, maximum 100 characters to limit query complexity. Empty string is treated as no search filter.

account_status.description:
Optional array of account statuses to filter results. Valid values: 'active' (normal operation), 'suspended' (temporary restriction), 'terminated' (permanent ban), 'deleted' (user-initiated deletion).

If null or omitted, defaults to ['active'] for public queries to show only active members. Administrators may query multiple statuses simultaneously. Empty array includes all statuses without filtering.

email_verified.description:
Optional filter for email verification status. If true, only members with verified email addresses are returned. If false, only unverified members are returned. If null or omitted, both verified and unverified members are included in results.

Email verification indicates whether the member has completed the email verification process after registration. Null is the default, returning all members regardless of verification status.

sort_by.description:
Sort order for member results. Valid values:

- 'created_at': Sort by account creation time (newest members first) - default value
- 'display_name': Sort alphabetically by public display name
- 'last_login_at': Sort by last login timestamp (recently active members first)
- 'article_count': Sort by number of articles created (most prolific contributors first)

Default: 'created_at' for reverse chronological ordering of newest members first.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction for results. Valid values:

- 'asc': Ascending order (A-Z, oldest to newest, smallest to largest)
- 'desc': Descending order (Z-A, newest to oldest, largest to smallest)

Default: 'desc' for reverse chronological order showing most recent items first.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1. Each page contains up to 'limit' number of results. Enables efficient paging through large result sets.

Default: 1 (first page). Must be a positive integer. Invalid page numbers may return empty results or the last available page depending on implementation.

limit.description:
Number of member results per page. Maximum 100 to prevent excessive data retrieval in single request. Enables clients to control result set size based on UI requirements and bandwidth constraints.

Default: 20 results per page. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive. Larger values reduce pagination requests but increase response payload size.

articles.description: Array of article search results matching the search query. Each result includes article summary information optimized for display in search result lists. Results are ordered by relevance or chronological ordering based on search parameters and sorting configuration.

comments.description: Array of comment search results matching the search query. Each result includes comment summary information for display in search result lists. Results show comments that matched the search criteria with context for understanding relevance to the search query.

total_results.description: Total count of search results across all types (articles and comments combined). Indicates total number of matching items for pagination and result scope understanding. Enables clients to understand the full scope of search results.

result_types.description: Breakdown of result counts by type showing how many articles and comments matched the search query separately. Supports UI filtering and result categorization by content type. Enables clients to understand the composition of search results and navigate between different result types.

IDiscussionBoardSearchResult.description:
Unified search results combining articles and comments matching a search query.

Provides comprehensive search results across both article and comment content types in a single response. Search results enable members to discover relevant discussions by keyword search across the discussion board content. The unified format supports efficient content discovery alongside category browsing and member navigation.

Results include article and comment summaries optimized for efficient display in search result interfaces. Result counts and type breakdowns support UI rendering and allow users to understand result composition and navigate between different result types. Each result maintains references to author member information and category classification for context.

email.description:
New email address for the member account. Must be validated for proper RFC 5322 email format with maximum 254 characters. Must be unique across all member accounts to prevent duplicate registrations.

Email changes can trigger verification requirements depending on business logic. Email is used for authentication, password recovery, and platform communications.

Optional field - omit to keep existing email unchanged.

username.description:
New username for the member account. Must maintain case-insensitive uniqueness across all members. Used as alternative login credential alongside email.

Username must be 3-30 characters long containing only alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens. Displayed in search results and used for public identification.

Optional field - omit to keep existing username unchanged.

display_name.description:
New public-facing display name for article and comment attribution. Must be 1-50 characters. Updates how the member's name appears to other platform users when they view articles and comments.

May differ from the username and can contain spaces and special characters for more natural-sounding names.

Optional field - omit to keep existing display name unchanged.

password.description:
New password for the member account (plain text - backend hashes using bcrypt minimum 12 rounds before storage). Password updates should typically use dedicated password change endpoints with additional security verification.

The password must meet complexity requirements defined by business rules before being hashed and stored securely.

Optional field - omit to keep existing password unchanged.

account_status.description:
Updated account status controlling member access and participation privileges.

- 'active': Normal operation with full posting and commenting privileges
- 'suspended': Temporary restriction due to policy violations or moderation action
- 'terminated': Permanent ban from the platform
- 'deleted': User-initiated deletion of account (soft delete with audit trail)

Changes to this status affect whether the member can authenticate and participate in discussions.

Optional field - omit to keep existing account status unchanged.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IUpdate.description:
Partial member account update request containing only the fields to be modified. All fields are optional - only include fields that should be changed.

This DTO enables updating member profile information (email, username, display_name) and account management fields (password, account_status). The update operation validates all provided values according to business rules and enforces unique constraints on email and username fields.

Password updates are hashed server-side using bcrypt (minimum 12 rounds) before storage. Account status changes control member access privileges - 'active' grants full access, 'suspended' restricts access temporarily, 'terminated' implements permanent bans, and 'deleted' implements soft deletion.

Systematic field-by-field updates are supported - only modified fields need to be included in the request. Unmodified fields are left unchanged, allowing for granular member account management without requiring all fields in each request.

Note: Timestamp fields (created_at, updated_at, last_login_at, deleted_at) are system-managed and cannot be modified through this DTO. Authentication context fields are populated automatically from the authenticated user session.

id.description: Unique identifier for the member profile record. Corresponds one-to-one with the member account.

member_id.description: Foreign key reference to the associated member account in the discussion_board_members table.

display_name.description: The name displayed publicly on the member's profile and next to their articles and comments. Must be 1-50 characters. May differ from the username and can contain spaces and special characters for more natural-sounding presentation.

bio.description:
A brief biographical description or profile blurb written by the member. Displayed on their public profile page. Optional field - can be null if the member has not provided biographical information.

When provided, bio is limited to maximum 500 characters. Members can use this to introduce themselves and share relevant expertise or interests related to economic and political discussions. Typically 160-500 characters for meaningful content.

profile_picture_url.description:
URL pointing to the member's profile picture image. Displayed as an avatar throughout the platform on articles, comments, and profile pages. Null if the member has not uploaded a profile picture, in which case a default avatar is typically displayed.

Images are automatically resized to 200x200 pixels and EXIF metadata is stripped during upload for privacy protection.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the member profile record was created, typically when the member account was initially registered.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the member profile was last updated, including changes to display_name, bio, or profile picture.

IDiscussionBoardMemberProfile.description:
Extended profile information for a member account. Contains personal presentation data including display name, biographical information, and profile picture.

The profile is created when the member account is registered and can be updated by the member to personalize their public presence on the discussion board platform. The profile picture is optional and can be added or changed at any time.

Biographical information and profile pictures are optional fields that members can add to enhance their public profile. All profile modifications are tracked through the updated_at timestamp for audit purposes.

display_name.description: Updated public display name to be shown as author attribution on articles and comments. Must be between 1-50 characters. This value will replace the existing display_name in the member's profile.

bio.description: Updated biographical information or 'about me' text. Optional field with maximum 500 characters. Can be set to null to remove biographical information from the profile. Used to introduce the member and share relevant expertise for economic and political discussions.

profile_picture_url.description: Updated URL reference to the member's profile picture in the attachment system. Must be a valid URI pointing to an image file that has been stored through the attachment upload system. Can be set to null to remove the profile picture. Images are automatically resized to 200x200 pixels with EXIF metadata stripped.

IDiscussionBoardMemberProfile.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating a member's profile information.

Allows authenticated members to modify their public-facing profile data including display name, biographical content, and profile picture URL. All fields are optional, allowing partial updates of profile information.

The display name must comply with length restrictions (1-50 characters) and the bio is limited to 500 characters maximum. The profile_picture_url must be a valid URI if provided. When the profile is successfully updated, the updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current UTC time, providing an audit trail of modifications.

This update operation is restricted to the profile owner and enforces authorization checks to ensure members can only modify their own profile information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the member preference record. Primary key in the discussion_board_member_preferences table.

member_id.description: Reference to the member account these preferences belong to. Each member has exactly one preference record. Links to discussion_board_members.id.

email_notifications_enabled.description: Master toggle for all email notifications. When false, no email notifications are sent regardless of other preference settings. Default: true to enable notifications. Members can disable to reduce inbox volume.

comment_reply_notifications.description: Whether member receives email notifications when someone replies to their comments. Default: true. Only active if email_notifications_enabled is true.

article_reply_notifications.description: Whether member receives email notifications when someone comments on their articles. Default: true. Only active if email_notifications_enabled is true.

article_approval_notifications.description: Whether member receives email notifications when their submitted articles are approved or rejected by moderators. Default: true. Helps members track publication status of their submissions.

moderator_action_notifications.description: Whether member receives email notifications about moderator actions affecting their content (deletions, edits, etc.). Default: true. Only applies if member's content is actioned by moderators.

daily_digest_enabled.description: Whether member receives optional daily digest emails summarizing new articles and discussions. Default: false (disabled). When enabled, digest is sent daily at a consistent time.

oneOf.description: Preferred display theme for the user interface. Valid values: 'light', 'dark', 'system'. Default: 'system' (follows system preference). Stored as lowercase string for consistent comparison.
Preferred display theme for the user interface. Valid values: 'light', 'dark', 'system'. Default: 'system' (follows system preference). Stored as lowercase string for consistent comparison.
Preferred display theme for the user interface. Valid values: 'light', 'dark', 'system'. Default: 'system' (follows system preference). Stored as lowercase string for consistent comparison.

display_theme.description: Preferred display theme for the user interface. Valid values: 'light', 'dark', 'system'. Default: 'system' (follows system preference). Stored as lowercase string for consistent comparison.

created_at.description: Timestamp when preference record was created (typically when member account was created). All preferences are initialized with defaults at account creation time. Stored in UTC.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last preference modification. Updated whenever any preference setting is changed by the member. Used for audit trail of preference changes. Stored in UTC.

IDiscussionBoardMemberPreference.description:
Member account preferences and settings for notifications, display, and communication.

Stores personal preference settings that control how members receive notifications, display content, and interact with the platform. Each member has exactly one preference record that stores their individual settings for email notifications, notification frequency, display theme, and other personal preferences.

Notification preferences include options to control email notifications for article replies, comment replies, moderator actions, and optional daily digest emails. Display preferences include theme selection (light, dark, system default). All preferences have sensible defaults to provide a good out-of-the-box experience while allowing members to customize based on their needs.

Preference modifications are tracked through timestamps for audit purposes. These preferences are separate from profile data to maintain clear separation between public identity (profile) and private settings (preferences).

email_notifications_enabled.description: Master toggle for all email notifications. When false, no email notifications are sent regardless of other preference settings. Members can disable to reduce inbox volume.

comment_reply_notifications.description: Whether member receives email notifications when someone replies to their comments. Only active if email_notifications_enabled is true.

article_reply_notifications.description: Whether member receives email notifications when someone comments on their articles. Only active if email_notifications_enabled is true.

article_approval_notifications.description: Whether member receives email notifications when their submitted articles are approved or rejected by moderators.

moderator_action_notifications.description: Whether member receives email notifications about moderator actions affecting their content (deletions, edits, etc.).

daily_digest_enabled.description: Whether member receives optional daily digest emails summarizing new articles and discussions.

oneOf.description: Preferred display theme for the user interface. Valid values: 'light', 'dark', 'system'. Stored as lowercase string for consistent comparison.
Preferred display theme for the user interface. Valid values: 'light', 'dark', 'system'. Stored as lowercase string for consistent comparison.
Preferred display theme for the user interface. Valid values: 'light', 'dark', 'system'. Stored as lowercase string for consistent comparison.

display_theme.description: Preferred display theme for the user interface. Valid values: 'light', 'dark', 'system'. Stored as lowercase string for consistent comparison.

IDiscussionBoardMemberPreference.IUpdate.description:
Update request for member notification and display preferences.

Allows members to modify their personal preference settings including notification controls and display theme. All fields are optional, allowing partial updates where only the preferences the member wishes to change need to be provided.

Notification preference fields control email notification delivery including toggles for comment replies, article replies, article approvals, moderator actions, and daily digest emails. Display theme can be set to light, dark, or system default preference.

Updates are recorded with an updated_at timestamp to track when preferences were last modified for audit purposes.

currentPassword.description: Member's current password in plain text for verification. Used to authenticate that the requester has legitimate access to this account before allowing password change. Compared against the stored password_hash using bcrypt verification. Maximum 128 characters.

newPassword.description:
New password for the member's account. Must meet strict complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters, maximum 128 characters, must contain at least one uppercase letter (A-Z), at least one lowercase letter (a-z), at least one numeric digit (0-9), and at least one special character from the set (!@#$%^&*).

Restrictions: Cannot contain the member's username or email address, cannot match any of the user's last 3 passwords (password reuse prevention).

Upon successful validation, the password is hashed using bcrypt with a minimum of 12 salt rounds before storage in the password_hash field.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IUpdatePassword.description:
Request body for updating a member's password with current password verification and new password meeting complexity requirements.

This DTO is used in PUT /discussionBoard/member/members/{memberId}/password operations to change an authenticated member's password. The member must provide their current password for verification and a new password that meets all security complexity requirements.

Password complexity is strictly enforced: minimum 8 characters, maximum 128 characters, must include uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numeric digits, and special characters. The system rejects weak passwords that lack required character types or are too short.

Security measures include password reuse prevention (cannot reuse any of last 3 passwords), username/email string prevention (password cannot contain username or email address), and bcrypt hashing with minimum 12 salt rounds before storage.

Note: This DTO only accepts plain text passwords. The backend performs all hashing and validation. Passwords are never stored, transmitted, or returned in any unencrypted form in responses.

memberId.description: Unique identifier of the member whose password was successfully changed. This confirms the operation was performed on the correct member account.

email.description: Member's email address. Used for account identification in the response. Maximum 254 characters.

displayName.description: Member's public-facing display name shown as author attribution on articles and comments. Provided in response for account confirmation. 1-50 characters.

passwordChangedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC indicating when the password was successfully changed. Used to confirm the operation completion time and for audit trail purposes.

sessionInvalidatedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC indicating when all existing authentication sessions were invalidated. Upon successful password change, all active sessions across all devices are immediately terminated to force re-authentication using the new password. This is a critical security measure.

message.description: User-friendly confirmation message indicating successful password change and session invalidation across all devices. Example: 'Password successfully updated. All sessions have been invalidated. Please log in again on your other devices.'

IDiscussionBoardMember.IPasswordChangeRe.description:
Response body confirming successful password change with account metadata and session invalidation confirmation.

This DTO is returned from PUT /discussionBoard/member/members/{memberId}/password operations after a member's password has been successfully updated. The response confirms the password change was completed and provides essential account and security information.

Key security confirmations: passwordChangedAt provides audit trail timestamp of when the change occurred, sessionInvalidatedAt confirms that all existing sessions have been terminated and the member must re-authenticate on all devices using their new password.

The response includes member identification (memberId, email, displayName) to confirm the operation was performed on the correct account. A user-friendly message explains the session invalidation requirement and prompts the member to log in again on their other devices.

Note: This response never includes the password, password hash, or any sensitive security data. The response is safe to log and audit without exposing credentials.

email.description: The new email address for the member account. Must be in valid RFC 5322 email format and be unique across all member accounts. Email addresses are case-insensitive for uniqueness checking. The maximum length is 254 characters as per RFC 5321 specification.

password.description: The member's current password for verification purposes. This security measure prevents unauthorized email hijacking by requiring the account holder to confirm their identity before allowing email changes. The password is verified against the stored password hash without being stored or logged.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IUpdateEmail.description: Request body for updating a member's email address. This operation requires password verification for security purposes to prevent unauthorized email hijacking. The new email address must be validated for proper RFC 5322 format and uniqueness across all member accounts. Upon successful update, the system sends a verification email to the new address containing a unique token valid for 24 hours. Until the member verifies the new email through the verification link or code, the previous email remains the active login credential.

name.description: The original filename of the profile picture provided by the member. This is preserved for audit purposes and stored in the attachment record metadata. The filename is extracted from the upload but does not determine the stored filename, which is system-generated for security.

extension.description: The file extension of the profile picture indicating the image format. Supported formats are jpg, png, gif, and webp. The system validates the actual file format by inspecting the file header (magic number) rather than relying on this extension for security purposes to prevent disguised executable uploads.

url.description: Pre-uploaded profile picture file URL from the storage service. The image file must be in JPG, PNG, GIF, or WebP format and not exceed 5 MB in size. The URL should point to the file location where it has been uploaded to the secure attachment storage system. The system will validate the image content, resize it to 200x200 pixels, strip EXIF metadata for privacy, and compute a SHA-256 hash for integrity verification.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IUploadProfilePic.description: Request body for uploading a profile picture for a member account. This operation accepts a pre-uploaded image file URL and associates it with the member's profile. The image file must be in one of the supported formats (JPG, PNG, GIF, or WebP) and not exceed 5 MB.
