Upon successful upload, the system processes the image by resizing it to 200x200 pixels for consistent display, stripping EXIF metadata to protect privacy, and computing integrity verification hashes. The member's profile record is updated with the profile_picture_url, and a corresponding attachment record is created for audit tracking. If the member already has a profile picture, the new upload replaces the previous image.

verification_code.description: The alphanumeric verification code received by the member via email. This code was generated during member registration or resend verification request and must be submitted to complete the email verification process. The code is case-insensitive and valid for 24 hours from generation.

verification_token.description: Optional JWT-style token that was included in the verification email link. This token serves as an alternative to the verification_code and provides additional security through cryptographic validation. If both verification_code and verification_token are provided, either may be used for verification.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IVerifyEmail.description:
Request DTO for email verification during member registration workflow.

When members register for the discussion board, they must verify ownership of their email address by submitting the verification code or token they received via email. This DTO captures the verification credentials needed to complete the email verification process.

The verification code is the primary mechanism and can be entered manually by the member. The verification token is an optional cryptographic alternative that can be extracted from a verification link. At least one of these must be provided, with verification_code being required.

Upon successful verification, the member's email_verified flag is set to true, granting full posting privileges for article creation and comment posting.

message.description: Generic confirmation message indicating that the verification email has been sent. The message does not reveal whether the email was actually sent or if the account was already verified, providing security by preventing account enumeration attacks.

resend_available_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when the member can request another verification email resend. This field implements rate limiting (once per 5 minutes per member). If null, the member can immediately request another resend.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IResendVerificati.description:
Response DTO for the resend verification email operation.

This response confirms that the resend verification email request has been processed. The response uses generic messaging for security reasons—it returns success even if the member's email is already verified, preventing attackers from enumerating valid member accounts.

The resend_available_at field indicates when the next resend can be requested, enforcing a rate limit of once per 5 minutes per member account. If the member has not yet hit the rate limit, this field will be null, allowing immediate resends.

The member will receive a new verification email containing both a verification code (for manual entry) and verification token (for link-based verification). The new credentials invalidate any previously sent codes, preventing confusion from multiple valid codes in circulation.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IPasswordResetReq.description:
Request body for initiating password reset workflow for a discussion board member.

This DTO is used when a member has forgotten their password and needs to request a password reset. The member provides their email address, which the system validates to ensure an account exists with that email. A secure password reset token is generated and sent via email with a reset link.

Security considerations are built into the operation: the system does not reveal whether an account exists with the provided email address. This prevents account enumeration attacks. The confirmation response is identical regardless of whether the email exists, protecting user privacy and security.

Rate limiting is enforced on this operation - members can request password resets a maximum of once per 5 minutes per email address to prevent abuse and brute force attacks.

email.description: Member email address requesting password reset. This email must match exactly (case-insensitive) with a registered member account in the system. The system will validate that this email corresponds to an active member account before generating and sending the password reset token. Used for sending the password reset email containing the secure reset link and instructions.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IPasswordResetReq.description:
Response body for password reset request operation.

This response confirms that a password reset request has been processed. For security reasons, the response message is generic and does not reveal whether an account with the provided email address exists in the system. This prevents account enumeration attacks and protects user privacy.

When a valid email is provided (matching a registered member account), the system generates a cryptographically secure password reset token with 1-hour expiration and sends a password reset email containing a secure reset link and instructions. When an invalid email is provided (no matching account), the system still returns a success response with the same message to prevent revealing which email addresses are registered.

The password reset workflow is a two-step process: this request initiates the process by sending the reset email, and the member then completes the password reset by clicking the reset link in their email and confirming their new password via the password-reset-confirm endpoint.

message.description: Generic confirmation message indicating the password reset request has been processed. The message is identical regardless of whether the email address exists in the system, providing a secure response that does not reveal account enumeration information. The member should check their email inbox and spam folder for the password reset instructions.

reset_token.description: The password reset token received in the password reset email. This token was generated by the password-reset-request operation and has a validity window of 1 hour from generation. The token uniquely identifies the member and validates their identity for the password reset operation.

password.description: The new password for the member account. Must meet all complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters, at least one uppercase letter (A-Z), at least one lowercase letter (a-z), at least one numeric digit (0-9), and at least one special character from {!@#$%^&*}. The password cannot contain the member's email address or username. The password cannot match any of the member's last 3 passwords to prevent password reuse.

password_confirm.description: Confirmation of the new password. Must exactly match the password field. Used to prevent typos when entering the new password.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IPasswordResetCon.description: Request body for password reset confirmation operation. Contains the reset token received in the password reset email and the new password details. The system validates the token has not expired (1-hour window), has not been previously used, and verifies the new password meets all complexity requirements including minimum length, character diversity, and password history constraints.

success.description: Indicates the password reset was completed successfully. When true, the member's password has been updated, all existing sessions have been invalidated, and a confirmation email has been sent.

message.description: A user-friendly message describing the successful password reset operation. Indicates that the password has been changed and all sessions have been terminated.

member_id.description: The unique identifier of the member whose password was reset. Present only in successful responses. Can be used to reference the member in subsequent operations.

oneOf.description: Successful password reset response. Confirms that the password has been updated in the password_hash field, all existing sessions have been invalidated, and a confirmation email has been sent to the member's registered email address.

success.description: Indicates the password reset operation failed. When false, the password has not been changed and no sessions have been invalidated.

message.description: A user-friendly message describing the failure reason. For failed resets, provides specific guidance on what validation requirement was not met (e.g., token expired, password does not meet complexity requirements, passwords do not match).

oneOf.description: Failed password reset response. Indicates that the password reset operation could not be completed due to validation failures. Provides specific error message indicating the cause (token expiration, password complexity violation, mismatched password fields, or other validation failures).

IDiscussionBoardMember.IPasswordResetCon.description:
Response body for password reset confirmation operation. Uses a discriminated union pattern to represent two possible outcomes: successful password reset with member ID returned, or failed reset with specific error message.

For successful resets (success: true), returns the member ID and confirmation message indicating the password has been updated, all sessions have been invalidated, and a confirmation email has been sent.

For failed resets (success: false), returns only a message describing the specific validation failure (token expired, password complexity violation, password mismatch, etc.), enabling the client to guide the user toward resolution.

current_password.description:
The member's current password in plain text for verification. Must be at least 8 characters long. This password is verified against the stored password_hash using bcrypt hash comparison to prevent unauthorized password changes. The verification ensures that only the account holder can initiate a password change.

The current password must match what the member originally set or last changed their password to. If the current password is incorrect, the operation returns an error without revealing the password was wrong (preventing account enumeration attacks).

new_password.description: The new password that meets all security complexity requirements. Must be at least 8 characters long and include at least one uppercase letter, at least one lowercase letter, at least one numeric digit, and at least one special character from the set: !@#$%^&*. The new password cannot be a commonly used password, cannot contain the member's username or email address, and cannot match any of the member's previous 3 passwords to prevent password reuse vulnerabilities.

password_confirm.description: Confirmation of the new password. Must exactly match the new_password field character-for-character. Used to prevent typos when entering the new password. If the new_password and password_confirm do not match, the operation returns an error and requires the user to re-enter both password fields.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IChangePassword.description:
Request body for changing an authenticated member's account password. Contains the current password for verification and the new password with confirmation, both of which must meet all complexity requirements. Upon successful password change, all existing sessions for the member are invalidated for security purposes, forcing re-authentication on all devices.

The operation directly modifies the password_hash field in the discussion_board_members table using bcrypt hashing with a minimum of 12 salt rounds. This ensures secure password storage and prevents unauthorized account access.

Password confirmation is required to prevent accidental typos when setting a new password. Both the new password and confirmation must match exactly and must satisfy all password complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, numeric, and special character diversity.

message.description: Confirmation message indicating that the password has been successfully changed and all sessions have been invalidated. Typical message: 'Password changed successfully. All sessions have been invalidated. Please log in again on your devices.'

success.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the password change operation was successful. True indicates the password was changed and sessions were invalidated; false indicates the operation failed.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IChangePasswordRe.description:
Response body confirming successful password change and session invalidation. Indicates that the member's password has been securely updated in the password_hash field and all existing sessions have been removed from the discussion_board_member_sessions table. The member must re-authenticate on all devices with the new password.

This response confirms that the security measures have been applied, preventing access from previously authenticated devices and protecting the account from compromised sessions.

token.description: JWT access token to be validated. This is the Bearer token string that was issued during member authentication. The token contains encrypted claims including member ID, email, username, and role information. The server will verify the token signature using HMAC-SHA256 with the server's signing secret to ensure the token has not been tampered with or forged.

IDiscussionBoardMemberSession.IValidateT.description: Request body for token validation operation. Contains the JWT access token that needs to be validated for authenticity, integrity, and current validity. This allows clients to verify token state before making API requests, enabling optimized token refresh decisions.

valid.description: Indicates whether the JWT access token passed all validation checks. Valid tokens have authentic signatures, have not been tampered with, contain all required claims, and have not expired.

reason.description: Detailed explanation of token validation status. For valid tokens, this explains what passed validation. For invalid tokens, this provides specific reason for failure (e.g., 'expired', 'invalid_signature', 'malformed', 'missing_claims') to help clients understand what happened and determine appropriate action (e.g., trigger token refresh).

expired.description: Indicates whether the token has exceeded its expiration timestamp. Valid tokens will have expired: false. Expired tokens trigger client-side token refresh via the refresh endpoint.

oneOf.description: Decoded JWT claims from the token when validation is successful
Null when token validation fails due to invalid signature, malformation, or missing required claims

claims.description: Decoded JWT claims from the token if validation was successful. Contains member identification and role information extracted from the token's payload. Only present when the token has valid signature and is not malformed. The claims object contains the authenticated member's ID, email, username, role designation, and token lifetime metadata (issued-at and expiration timestamps). When validation fails, this field is null or absent.

IDiscussionBoardMemberSession.IValidatio.description:
Response body from token validation operation. Provides comprehensive validation results including token validity status, specific failure reasons, expiration status, and decoded claims if the token is valid.

This response allows clients to understand exactly why a token is invalid and decide whether to refresh it via the refresh endpoint, re-authenticate with login credentials, or prompt the user to log in again. The response contains three always-present fields (valid, reason, expired) and an optional claims object that is only populated when the token passes all validation checks.

When valid: true, the claims field contains the decoded member identification and role information. When valid: false, the reason field provides specific diagnostic information and claims is null. The expired field independently indicates whether the token has exceeded its exp timestamp, allowing clients to distinguish between expired tokens and other validation failures.

member_id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated member. This is the UUID primary key from the discussion_board_members table, identifying which member issued and owns this session token.

email.description: Member's registered email address. Used for communication and account identification. Matches the email stored in the discussion_board_members table.

username.description: Member's unique username for display and authentication purposes. Identifies the member in discussion board interactions and login.

role.description: Member's role in the discussion board system determining their permissions and capabilities. Valid values are 'member' for regular users with standard permissions to create articles, post comments, and interact with community content, or 'moderator' for administrative users with content moderation capabilities (approving articles, managing user violations) and system management permissions.

iat.description: Token issuance timestamp in Unix epoch seconds (seconds since January 1, 1970 UTC). Indicates when the token was created and issued to the member. Used to track token age and implement token rotation policies.

exp.description: Token expiration timestamp in Unix epoch seconds. The token becomes invalid after this time and clients must obtain a new token via the refresh endpoint or re-authenticate via login. Allows servers to enforce session lifetime limits and security policies.

IDiscussionBoardMemberSession.ITokenClai.description:
Decoded JWT claims from a valid member session token. Contains member identification information and token lifetime metadata extracted from the token's payload after cryptographic signature verification.

These claims identify the authenticated member and determine their permissions in the discussion board system. The iat (issued-at) and exp (expiration) timestamps enable servers and clients to enforce session lifetime policies and determine when tokens need refresh. This schema represents the standard JWT payload structure for discussion board member authentication.

All fields in this schema are present and non-null in valid tokens. If any required field is missing or malformed, the token validation will fail.

token.description: The moderator's access token in JWT format for validation. This is the Bearer token provided in the Authorization header without the 'Bearer ' prefix. Used to verify the moderator's authentication status and active session.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IValidateToken.description:
Request body for validating a moderator's authentication token and active session.

This DTO is used when a moderator wants to verify that their current access token is still valid and their associated session remains active. The token is validated against the moderator's session records to ensure the session has not been terminated or expired beyond the 7-day window.

The moderator typically sends this token as part of their regular API requests to determine if session refresh is needed or to maintain session continuity across protected resources.

is_valid.description:
Indicates whether the moderator's access token and associated session are currently active and valid. Returns true if the token signature is valid, not expired, and the corresponding session exists and has not been terminated. Returns false if any validation check fails.

When is_valid is true, all other fields in the response contain complete and current moderator and session information. When is_valid is false, the remaining fields may be null or contain incomplete information, as validation failed before full session data could be retrieved.

oneOf.description: Unique identifier of the moderator whose token was validated. This is extracted from the JWT claims (userId field) and is populated when token validation is successful.
When token validation fails, this field is null as the moderator ID cannot be reliably extracted from an invalid or expired token.

moderator_id.description: Unique identifier of the moderator whose token was validated. This is extracted from the JWT claims (userId field) when the token signature and claims are valid. If validation fails (is_valid is false), this field is null because the moderator identity cannot be confirmed from an invalid token.

oneOf.description: Username of the authenticated moderator. Extracted from the JWT token claims (username field) when validation succeeds.
Null when token validation fails or token claims cannot be extracted.

username.description: Username of the authenticated moderator. Extracted from the JWT token claims (username field) and identifies the moderator by their login username. Only populated when the token validation succeeds (is_valid is true). Returns null if validation fails.

oneOf.description: Display name of the moderator shown in moderation interface and audit logs. Extracted from JWT token claims.
Null when token validation fails.

display_name.description: Display name of the moderator. Extracted from the JWT token claims (displayName field) when validation succeeds. This is the name displayed in the moderation interface and audit logs. Returns null if validation fails (is_valid is false).

oneOf.description: Email address of the authenticated moderator extracted from JWT token claims when validation succeeds.
Null when token validation fails.

email.description: Email address of the authenticated moderator. Extracted from the JWT token claims when validation succeeds. Used for communication and as part of the moderator's identity in the system. Returns null if validation fails (is_valid is false).

role.description: Authorization role of the authenticated user. Always 'moderator' for this validation endpoint. Indicates that this token belongs to a moderator with elevated permissions for content moderation and user management.

oneOf.description: Boolean indicating email verification status at the time the token was issued. Extracted from JWT token claims (emailVerified field).
Null when token validation fails.

email_verified.description: Indicates whether the moderator's email address has been verified. Extracted from the JWT token claims (emailVerified field) when validation succeeds. Shows the email verification status at the time the token was issued. Returns null if validation fails (is_valid is false).

oneOf.description: The moderator account is active in the discussion_board_moderators table and has full access permissions.
The moderator account is suspended in the discussion_board_moderators table. Even if the token appears valid, validation fails when status is 'suspended'.
The moderator account is permanently terminated in the discussion_board_moderators table. Validation fails immediately when status is 'terminated'.
Null when token validation fails or account status cannot be retrieved.

account_status.description: Current account status of the moderator in the discussion_board_moderators table. Shows whether the moderator account is active, suspended, or permanently terminated. Only 'active' status allows validation to succeed. If the status is not 'active', the validation fails even if the token appears valid. Returns null if validation fails (is_valid is false).

oneOf.description: Unique identifier of the active moderator session. This session must exist in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table with a null expired_at value indicating an active, non-terminated session.
Null when the session does not exist or validation fails.

session_id.description: Unique identifier of the active moderator session associated with the token. This session must exist in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table with a null expired_at value (indicating an active, non-terminated session). Returns null if no active session exists or if validation fails (is_valid is false).

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the validated session was created, stored in discussion_board_moderator_sessions.created_at. Used to verify the session is within the 7-day expiration window.
Null when session validation fails.

session_created_at.description: Timestamp when the validated session was created. Stored in discussion_board_moderator_sessions.created_at. Used to verify the session is within the 7-day expiration window. Returns null if validation fails or session cannot be retrieved (is_valid is false).

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the access token was issued, extracted from the iat (issued-at) claim in the JWT. Indicates when the moderator authenticated and obtained this token.
Null when token validation fails.

token_issued_at.description: Timestamp when the access token was issued (iat claim in JWT). Indicates when the moderator authenticated and obtained this token. Returns null if token validation fails (is_valid is false).

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the access token will expire, extracted from the exp (expiration) claim in the JWT. After this time, the token becomes invalid.
Null when token validation fails.

token_expires_at.description: Timestamp when the access token will expire (exp claim in JWT). After this time, the token becomes invalid and the moderator must refresh or re-authenticate. Returns null if token validation fails (is_valid is false).

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ITokenValidati.description:
Response body containing the result of a moderator token validation check and associated session details.

Returned when a moderator validates their authentication token to verify it is still valid and their session remains active. The response includes comprehensive token and session information that allows the client to determine whether the moderator needs to refresh their session or re-authenticate.

Validation Process: The system performs the following checks: (1) JWT signature verification using the configured signing secret, (2) token expiration check by comparing the exp claim against current time, (3) session existence verification in discussion_board_moderator_sessions table, (4) session status verification (expired_at must be null), and (5) moderator account status verification in discussion_board_moderators table (must be 'active').

Response Behavior Based on Validation Result:
- When is_valid is true: All fields contain complete and current information. The moderator's session is active and valid within the 7-day window. All moderator details, session information, and token timestamps are fully populated and reliable.
- When is_valid is false: Some fields are null as extraction failed. The moderator_id, username, display_name, email, email_verified, session_id, session_created_at, token_issued_at, and token_expires_at fields are null because validation failed before full data could be retrieved. Only the role field is always populated as 'moderator'. This allows clients to distinguish between validation success and failure states.

id.description: Unique identifier for the warning record. Auto-generated by the system as a UUID primary key.

member_id.description: Unique identifier of the member account that received the warning. References the discussion_board_members table to identify which member is being warned.

moderator_id.description: Unique identifier of the moderator who issued the warning. References the discussion_board_moderators table to track which moderator took the action.

oneOf.description: Formal warning issued to member without restricting access. Warning accumulates in moderation history but does not expire or auto-reactivate.
Temporary account restriction preventing login and posting. Suspension automatically expires and reactivates account at suspension_end_date.
Permanent account closure. Termination does not auto-reactivate and represents final removal of member from system.

action_type.description: Type of disciplinary action taken on the member account. Values include 'warning' for formal warnings, 'suspension' for temporary account restrictions, and 'termination' for permanent account closure.

reason.description: Business reason for the disciplinary action. Describes the policy violation or guideline breach that triggered the warning. Can reference specific problematic behavior or violation category. Required for all warning types.

notes.description: Optional detailed moderator notes providing context and internal documentation for other moderators. May reference specific articles, comments, or previous violations to establish escalation patterns.

suspension_end_date.description: End date and time for temporary suspension in UTC format. Only populated when action_type is 'suspension'. The system automatically reactivates the member account at this timestamp. Null for warning or termination actions.

is_active.description: Whether this warning, suspension, or termination is currently in effect. For warnings: always TRUE (warnings don't expire). For suspensions: TRUE while active, changes to FALSE when suspension expires and auto-reactivation occurs. For terminations: always TRUE (terminations are permanent). Used to determine current status of disciplinary action without comparing timestamps.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the warning record was created, automatically set by the system to the current UTC datetime.

member.description: Summary information about the member who received the warning, including their display name and account status.

moderator.description: Summary information about the moderator who issued the warning, including their username and moderator status.

IDiscussionBoardUserWarning.description:
User warning record representing disciplinary actions taken against discussion board members. This entity maintains a complete audit trail of warnings, suspensions, and terminations issued by moderators.

Warnings serve as the primary enforcement mechanism for policy violations and community guideline breaches. They accumulate in a member's history, allowing moderators to track escalation patterns and ensure consistent enforcement of community standards.

Each warning record captures the member receiving the action, the moderator issuing it, the type of action taken (warning, suspension, or termination), the business reason for the action, and optional detailed notes for other moderators' reference.

For suspension actions, the suspension_end_date specifies when the account will be automatically reactivated. The system prevents suspended members from logging in or posting content until the suspension period expires.

The is_active field indicates whether the disciplinary action is currently in effect. For warnings, this remains permanently TRUE. For suspensions, this changes to FALSE when the suspension period expires and the account auto-reactivates. For terminations, this remains permanently TRUE.

Warning records are immutable once created and serve as permanent documentation of disciplinary history, enabling informed decisions for future escalations.

oneOf.description: Type of disciplinary action to be taken. Values include 'warning' for formal warnings, 'suspension' for temporary account restrictions, and 'termination' for permanent account closure.
Type of disciplinary action to be taken. Values include 'warning' for formal warnings, 'suspension' for temporary account restrictions, and 'termination' for permanent account closure.
Type of disciplinary action to be taken. Values include 'warning' for formal warnings, 'suspension' for temporary account restrictions, and 'termination' for permanent account closure.

action_type.description: Type of disciplinary action to be taken. Values include 'warning' for formal warnings, 'suspension' for temporary account restrictions, and 'termination' for permanent account closure.

reason.description: Business reason for the disciplinary action. Must describe the policy violation or guideline breach that triggered the warning. Can reference specific problematic behavior, violation category ('Repeated Violations', 'Harassment', 'Spam', 'Hate Speech', 'Copyright Violation'), or custom explanation. Required field.

notes.description: Optional detailed moderator notes providing internal context and documentation. May reference specific articles, comments, or previous violations to establish escalation rationale. Helps other moderators understand the decision and track patterns.

suspension_end_date.description: End date and time for temporary suspension in UTC format. REQUIRED when action_type is 'suspension'. Must be a future timestamp. The system automatically reactivates the member account at this date/time. FORBIDDEN for warning or termination action types - set to null for non-suspension actions.

IDiscussionBoardUserWarning.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new warning, suspension, or termination record for a member account. This DTO captures moderator-issued disciplinary actions in response to policy violations or guideline breaches.

The moderator must specify the action type (warning, suspension, or termination) and provide a business reason (10-500 characters) explaining the violation. Optional moderator notes (up to 1000 characters) allow detailed context-setting for other moderators reviewing this member's history.

For suspension actions only, the moderator must specify suspension_end_date as a future UTC timestamp. The system uses this date to automatically reactivate the account. For warning or termination actions, suspension_end_date must be null.

Moderator identity (moderator_id) and affected member identity (member_id) are provided by the authenticated session and path parameters respectively - they are NOT included in this request body.

Warning records are immediately persisted and notification emails are sent to the affected member explaining the action and its consequences.

reason.description: Detailed moderator-provided reason for the permanent account ban. Explains why the member's account is being terminated and what policy violations led to this decision. Minimum 10 characters, maximum 500 characters. This reason is recorded in the audit trail and communicated to the banned member via email notification, ensuring transparency in the moderation decision.

oneOf.description: Optional internal moderator notes up to 1000 characters for detailed context about the ban decision. May contain references to specific violations, pattern analysis, or escalation factors. Not shown to the banned member but available to other moderators and administrators. Null if no additional notes are needed.
No additional notes provided for this ban decision.

notes.description:
Optional internal moderator notes up to 1000 characters for detailed context about the ban decision. May contain references to specific violations, pattern analysis, or escalation factors. Not shown to the banned member but available to other moderators and administrators for understanding decision rationale.

When null, indicates no additional context notes were recorded. This field supports optional detailed documentation of the ban reasoning for internal moderation team awareness and pattern analysis across multiple ban decisions.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IBan.description:
Ban action request for permanently terminating a member account.

Contains the moderator's detailed ban reason and optional notes explaining why the member's account is being permanently terminated. The ban is irreversible without administrator intervention and sets the member's account status to 'terminated', preventing all future access to the platform.

The reason provided is communicated to the banned member via email notification, ensuring they understand the decision. Notes are retained internally for moderation pattern analysis and audit purposes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the moderation action record.

moderatorId.description: Reference to the moderator who performed this moderation action. Essential for audit trail and accountability, enabling tracking of which moderator approved, rejected, deleted, or edited content. Links to discussion_board_moderators.id.

memberId.description: Reference to the member whose content was moderated (article or comment author). Used to track and notify which member's content was moderated and enables understanding the impact of moderation decisions on specific community members. Links to discussion_board_members.id.

oneOf.description: Type of moderation action that was performed. Approved indicates article was reviewed and published for community viewing.
Type of moderation action that was performed. Rejected indicates article was not approved for publication and did not proceed to community.
Type of moderation action that was performed. Requested changes means moderator provided feedback for revision before approval decision.
Type of moderation action that was performed. Deleted article indicates article was removed from platform due to violation.
Type of moderation action that was performed. Deleted comment indicates comment was removed due to violation.
Type of moderation action that was performed. Edited article means moderator corrected article content directly.
Type of moderation action that was performed. Edited comment means moderator corrected comment content directly.
Type of moderation action that was performed. Flagged indicates content was marked for further review by other moderators.

action_type.description: Type of moderation action that was performed. Determines business outcome, what notifications are sent to the affected member, and how the content flows through the system.

IDiscussionBoardReport.description:
Discussion board report entity representing member-submitted reports of inappropriate content.

Reports provide the moderation system with community feedback on content that may violate guidelines. Each report documents what content is reported (articles or comments), who reported it (reporter), the reason category, optional detailed description, and tracks the complete moderation workflow from submission through resolution.

Reports progress through the moderation workflow: pending_review (initial state when report is created) → resolved (moderator took action on content) or dismissed (moderator reviewed and determined no violation). The reporter and assigned_moderator are provided as transformed reference objects containing complete context.

The report maintains a complete audit trail including reporter identity, assigned moderator, resolution status, moderator investigation notes, and timestamps. This enables accountability, consistent decision-making, pattern analysis, and comprehensive moderation history tracking.

IDiscussionBoardReport.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new content report. Members submit this data when reporting an article or comment they believe violates community guidelines.

The report creation captures the reason category (required, must be one of the predefined enum values) and optional detailed description (maximum 500 characters) explaining the member's concern. The reporting member's identity is automatically captured from the authentication context and should not be provided in this request.

The reported content reference (article_id or comment_id) is provided via the API path parameter (/articles/{articleId}/reports or /comments/{commentId}/reports), not in this request body. The report is created with pending_review status, null moderator assignment, and null resolved_at timestamp, entering the moderation review queue for moderator investigation and action.

Unique identifier of the moderator to assign to this report for investigation and review. When provided, assigns responsibility for investigating this report to the specified moderator. The moderator is identified from their record in the discussion_board_moderators table. Null assignment is used when removing a moderator assignment (returning report to unassigned state).

This field is used by the assign endpoint to set which moderator is responsible for reviewing and resolving the reported content. Once assigned, the moderator can add notes and take final action to resolve or dismiss the report.

moderator_notes.description:
Notes added by moderator during investigation and review. Maximum 500 characters. Records moderator's findings, investigation outcome, and reasoning for their decision regarding the reported content.

Moderators update these notes iteratively as they investigate the report. Notes become part of the permanent audit trail documenting the review process and decision-making.

IDiscussionBoardReport.IUpdate.description:
Update request for discussion board report allowing moderators to update assignment and investigation notes. This DTO is used when moderators need to update report information during their review and decision-making process.

All fields are optional, allowing partial updates. Moderators can assign themselves or other moderators to reports, and can add or update moderator notes multiple times throughout the investigation process.

The moderator performing the action is automatically identified from the authenticated JWT token. Assignment and note updates are tracked with updated_at timestamps for audit purposes.

oneOf.description: Report has been resolved - the moderator took action on the reported content. Use this status when content was deleted, edited, or when a warning/suspension was issued to the author. Indicates the moderator's investigation led to corrective action being taken.

Report has been dismissed - the moderator reviewed the content and determined no action is needed. Use this status when the reported content does not violate community guidelines, or the guideline interpretation differs from the reporter's concern. Indicates content is acceptable as-is.

status.description: Resolution status for the report. Transitions the report from pending_review to a final status. Choose 'resolved' when moderator took action on reported content (deletion, editing, or user discipline). Choose 'dismissed' when content was reviewed and determined compliant with guidelines.

moderator_notes.description: Moderator's final investigation findings and reasoning for the resolution decision. Minimum 1 character, maximum 500 characters. Explains what action was taken (or why no action was taken), why the content does or does not violate guidelines, and any relevant context discovered during investigation. This becomes part of the permanent audit trail and may be shared with the reporter and content author.

IDiscussionBoardReport.IResolve.description:
Resolution request for discussion board report completing the moderation review workflow. Moderators use this DTO when they have finished investigating a pending report and are ready to mark it as resolved or dismissed.

The status field determines the outcome: 'resolved' indicates the moderator took corrective action on the content or author, while 'dismissed' indicates the content was found compliant with guidelines. Moderator notes provide the final investigation findings and decision explanation for audit purposes and potential communication with the reporter and content author.

The authenticated moderator is automatically recorded as the resolver. Resolution timestamps are set automatically by the system.

moderator_notes.description: Detailed notes from the moderator explaining why the report is being dismissed and reasoning for determining the content does not violate community guidelines. Minimum 10 characters, maximum 500 characters. These notes become part of the permanent audit trail for accountability and consistency in moderation decisions.

IDiscussionBoardReport.IDismiss.description:
Request body for dismissing a discussion board report.

This DTO represents the moderator's determination that reported content does not violate community guidelines and should remain published. The dismissal is recorded with the moderator's reasoning and investigation findings.

The dismissal operation updates the report status from 'pending_review' to 'dismissed', records the moderator's identity and timestamp, and creates a permanent audit trail for future reference and consistency analysis.

IDiscussionBoardSystemSetting.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and filtering discussion board system settings.

This DTO allows moderators and administrators to discover configuration settings through pagination, search, filtering by setting characteristics, and flexible sorting options. All parameters are optional, allowing clients to request unfiltered/unsorted results or apply specific combinations of filters.

System settings control platform behavior including feature flags (enable_comments, enable_file_uploads), site metadata (site_name, site_description), moderation rules (require_article_approval, auto_moderate_comments), and rate limits (max_articles_per_day, max_comments_per_day). The search functionality enables finding settings by key or description, while filters narrow results by type or active status.

Pagination parameters (page, limit) enable browsing large configuration catalogs efficiently. Sorting options allow organizing results by creation date, modification date, or setting key for easier discovery. Only moderators and administrators with appropriate permissions can access system settings to prevent unauthorized configuration modifications.

IDiscussionBoardSystemSetting.description:
System-wide configuration and settings that control platform behavior and features.

Stores key-value pairs for application configuration, feature flags, and operational settings. Provides centralized management of system behavior without requiring code changes or redeployment. Administrators modify settings through admin panels to control platform features and behavior.

Common settings include site metadata (site_name, site_description, support_email), feature flags (enable_new_user_registrations, enable_comments, enable_file_uploads, enable_search), moderation settings (require_article_approval, auto_moderate_comments, spam_detection_enabled), rate limiting (max_articles_per_day, max_comments_per_day, max_comment_burst), and system behavior (maintenance_mode, maintenance_message, session_timeout_minutes).

Each setting consists of setting_key (unique identifier), setting_value (configuration value), setting_type (data type hint), description (administrator reference), is_active (whether currently applied), updated_by (moderator/admin who last modified), and timestamps for audit purposes.

The system_settings table is the single source of truth for configuration, eliminating the need to modify environment variables or restart the application. Changes are applied immediately or on next request depending on setting type and system design.

Contains the essential configuration parameters needed to add or register a new system setting in the discussion_board_system_settings table. The settingKey must be unique and identifies the configuration parameter being created.

The settingValue provides the actual configuration value in string format, parsed by the application based on the settingType hint (string, integer, boolean, or json). An optional description explains the setting's purpose and impact for administrative reference.

New settings default to active status (is_active = true), meaning they are immediately applied by the system. The creating moderator's identity and timestamps are automatically captured in the database by the application.

Common settings include site metadata (site_name, site_description, support_email), feature flags (enable_new_user_registrations, enable_comments, enable_file_uploads, enable_search), moderation settings (require_article_approval, auto_moderate_comments, spam_detection_enabled), rate limiting parameters (max_articles_per_day, max_comments_per_day, max_comment_burst), and system behavior controls (maintenance_mode, maintenance_message, session_timeout_minutes).

IDiscussionBoardSystemSetting.IUpdate.description:

Allows modification of configuration parameters that control application behavior, feature flags, and operational settings. The operation validates that the provided settingKey exists before processing updates. Audit information (updated_by timestamp and moderator identity) is captured server-side and not accepted in the request body.

Common settings that can be modified include site metadata, feature flags, moderation settings, rate limiting parameters, and system behavior controls. Changes take effect immediately or on next request depending on setting type and system design.

referrer.description: HTTP Referrer header value when login occurred. Indicates which page referred member to authentication. May be empty string if referrer unavailable.

expired_at.description: Session termination timestamp. Non-null when session ends (member logout or expiration). Null for active sessions. Sessions expire automatically after 7 days or when member explicitly logs out.

Authentication session representing a single login instance from a member.

Tracks connection context including IP address, referrer URL, and access page (href) for security auditing and fraud detection. Each session is created upon successful authentication and persists until logout or automatic expiration after 7 days.

Members can maintain multiple concurrent sessions across different devices or browsers. Sessions are immutable once created, with only expiration timestamp subject to modification.

Note: Member identification is maintained through authentication context (JWT), not exposed in the session response body for security purposes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the moderator session.

ip.description: IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) from which the moderator login originated. Critical for security monitoring of administrative access and detecting unauthorized login attempts.

href.description: Full URL/URI where moderator login occurred. Captures the entry point for moderation dashboard access.

referrer.description: HTTP Referrer header value when moderator login occurred. Indicates source of authentication request. May be empty string if referrer not available.

created_at.description: Session creation timestamp (login time) in UTC. Records when moderator authentication session was established. Immutable.

expired_at.description: Session termination timestamp. Non-null when session ends (moderator logout or automatic expiration). Null for active sessions. Sessions expire after 7 days or explicit logout.

moderator.description: Summary information about the moderator who owns this session.

IDiscussionBoardModeratorSession.ISummar.description:
Summary representation of a moderator authentication session. Captures session metadata including connection context (IP, URL, referrer), timing information, and moderator identification.

Sessions represent moderator logins from specific IP addresses and track the connection context for security and audit purposes. Sessions are critical for monitoring administrative access patterns and detecting unauthorized access attempts.

The summary includes all essential session information for tracking and auditing purposes without requiring full detailed records.

pending_articles_count.description: Total count of articles currently awaiting moderator approval. Articles with status 'pending_approval' are included. This metric helps moderators prioritize their review workload and understand current queue size.

pending_articles.description: Array of up to 10 most recent articles pending approval, sorted by creation date (newest first). Each article includes essential information for quick review decision-making including title, author, category, creation timestamp, and preview of content.

suspended_members_count.description: Total count of members currently in 'suspended' account status. Suspended members cannot create articles or comments but can log in to view their account. This count helps moderators understand enforcement activity scope.

terminated_members_count.description: Total count of members with 'terminated' account status (permanently banned). Terminated members cannot log in and have complete platform access revoked. This count reflects the severity of community guideline enforcement.

recent_moderation_actions.description: Array of up to 20 most recent moderation actions taken (approvals, rejections, deletions) sorted by date (newest first). Provides audit trail visibility and helps track moderation pattern consistency.

approval_rate.description: Percentage of submitted articles approved for publication in the current period (calculated from last 30 days of moderation actions). Expressed as a number from 0-100. Helps assess moderation stringency and platform publication rate.

deletion_rate.description: Percentage of existing content (articles and comments) deleted in the current period (last 30 days). Expressed as a number from 0-100. Indicates community guideline compliance and content cleanup frequency.

average_review_time_hours.description: Average time in hours between article submission and moderator decision (approval, rejection, or change request). Calculated from articles reviewed in the last 30 days. Helps track moderation team responsiveness and efficiency.

dashboard_last_refreshed.description: Timestamp when the dashboard data was last calculated. Indicates freshness of the displayed metrics and statistics. Users can use this to understand how current the information is.

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.description:
Comprehensive moderation dashboard aggregating all pending moderation tasks and system metrics.

Provides moderators with a unified interface displaying pending articles awaiting approval, member account status summaries, recent moderation actions for audit trail visibility, and performance metrics about moderation effectiveness.

The dashboard aggregates real-time data from multiple sources including the pending article queue (articles with status 'pending_approval'), member activity history showing suspended and terminated accounts, moderation action audit logs tracking all moderator decisions, and calculated metrics about approval rates, deletion patterns, and review turnaround times.

Designed to give moderators comprehensive situational awareness of platform moderation state, workload priority, and enforcement pattern consistency without requiring multiple separate API calls. Metrics help identify trends in community guideline violations and moderator efficiency.

IDiscussionBoardSearchResult.IResultType.description:
Breakdown of search result counts by type showing how many articles and comments matched the search query.

Provides a summary of result distribution across content types for UI filtering and result categorization. Enables clients to understand the composition of search results and navigate between different result types.

Used within search results to display result type statistics and support filtering by content type.

articles_count.description: Number of article results matching the search query. Count of articles that matched the search criteria for UI display and result composition understanding.

comments_count.description: Number of comment results matching the search query. Count of comments that matched the search criteria for UI display and result composition understanding.
